Lamar Jackson suffered a thumb injury in Week 8 against the Buffalo Bills and is on injured reserve, shifting the line for this game from Ravens -3 (the lookahead) to Jaguars -9.5. That move also comes after backup Tyler Huntley (turf toe) was ruled out for this game and third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano is dealing with an ankle injury. So, the Ravens are in a brutal spot as they look to get back over .500 (Baltimore is 4-4 this season) against the top team in the AFC South. Jacksonville is in a great spot to win the AFC South for the second season in a row, as no other team in the division has more than two wins in 2026. The Jags blew out the Indianapolis Colts – 42-7 – in Week 8, and they’re one of the best defenses in the league, ranking third in EPA/Play and eighth in success rate. Liam Coen’s team is a deserved favorite in this matchup, which could be a tough one to bet on with all the Baltimore injuries. Still, the SI Betting team has curated some picks for Week 9’s Thursday Night showdown, including player props for Lawrence and Derrick Henry. Here’s a breakdown of some of our favorite bets for the action to kick off the final week of the first half of the 2026 season. Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley are likely out for the game, and their third-string quarterback, Joe Fagnano, is also questionable due to an injury. If he can't go, the Ravens are going to be starting a quarterback who's not on their roster as of me writing this article on Monday night. That leaves the Ravens' only plan of attack being running the football. Unfortunately, they now have to face a Jaguars defense that ranks second in opponent rush EPA and seventh in opponent rush success rate, while giving up fewer yards per carry than any other defense in the league (3.4). I could maybe be convinced to take the points with the Ravens if they had an elite defense, but they're completely average on that side of the ball. Jaguars second-year running back Bhayshul Tuten has played a major role on offense this season, appearing in 55.3 percent of the team’s snaps while registering at least 12 carries in every game. Tuten also has six straight games with two or more receptions, finding the end zone three times through the air and four times overall in his last two games. Chris Rodriguez is also going to factor into the Jacksonville attack, but I’m buying Tuten at +115 to find the end zone on Thursday. While Baltimore is allowing just 3.8 yards per carry this season, it’s already allowed 10 rushing scores. This could be a run-heavy game script for the Jags since they’re nearly favored by double digits, and Tuten has six total scores in seven games in 2026. He should continue to see a ton of work as the Jaguars look to run away with the AFC South. A former No. 1 overall pick, Lawrence is in the MVP conversation this season, but he hasn’t been asked to throw the ball a ton with this Jaguars offense humming on the ground in 2026. Lawrence is averaging under 29 pass attempts per game in 2026, and he threw the ball just 14 times in a 42-7 win over Indianapolis in Week 8. Overall, the star quarterback has just two games (Weeks 5 and 6) where he even attempted 30 passes. So, with the Jaguars heavily favored on a short week, I expect a lighter workload for Lawrence against a Ravens team that has lost three straight and is staring down a lost season with Jackson sidelined. If this game turns into a blowout like the Colts matchup did, Lawrence may not even attempt 25 passes for the fourth time in eight games. This season, Derrick Henry has just four games with over 70 rushing yards, and he’s coming off three straight down performances with 58, 45 and 53 rushing yards, allowing just 3.5 yards per carry during that stretch. The Jaguars are going to stack the box against Henry with all of Baltimore’s quarterback issues, and Jacksonville held Jonathan Taylor to under 30 rushing yards in a blowout in Week 8. The game script isn’t going to be favorable for Henry, and he only saw 11 rushes in Week 8. Jacksonville ranks No. 1 in the NFL in EPA/Rush, allowing the fewest yards per carry (3.4) and total rushing yards (542) in the league this season. picks.blurb: Prediction For Jaguars' Huge Thursday Night Clash With the Baltimore Ravens - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football NFL Week 9 updates Luka has tight back Rivers to coach NC State CFB winners and losers (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect) Jason Klingensmith · Roundtable Sports Thu, November 5, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads When the NFL schedule was released in May, the Week 9 Thursday Night Football clash between the Jacksonville Jaguars and Baltimore Ravens looked like one of the season's marquee games. It was expected to be a matchup featuring two AFC heavyweights, one that would carry significant playoff implications. The Jaguars have held up their end of the bargain, racing out to a 5-2 record and looking like one of the NFL's elite teams. The Ravens, on the other hand, have fallen short of expectations. They are only 4-4 and in last place in the AFC North. Two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson returned in Week 8 from a three-game absence due to a high-ankle sprain, only to suffer a serious thumb injury on the first snap against the Buffalo Bills . Jackson's newest injury requires surgery and is expected to sideline him for the rest of the season , likely ending Baltimore's chances of reaching the Super Bowl. Jackson's backup, Tyler Huntley, also went down with a season-ending turf toe injury after replacing Jackson against Buffalo. Now Baltimore must turn to undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano, who will be making his first NFL start against a strong Jacksonville defense. Fagnano was also injured in the Bills' game, but has worked hard to play on Thursday night. On Wednesday, the Ravens traded for former Arizona Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett, who was just demoted to third-string after starting the team's first eight games. Brissett won't be ready to play against Jacksonville, leaving the offense in Fagnano's hands. The Jaguars must overcome their own injury issues to walk out of Baltimore with their sixth victory of the season. Jacksonville also suffered a pair of season-ending injuries in its Week 8 42-7 thrashing of the Indianapolis Colts. Run-stuffing defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton will miss the rest of the year after tearing his quad. Starting safety Eric Murray joined Hamilton on injured reserve with an elbow injury. Running back Bhayshul Tuten, who is having a phenomenal season, is a game-time decision after not practicing all week with ankle and foot injuries. Star edge rusher Travon Walker is questionable with a rib ailment, though he got in limited practices on Tuesday and Wednesday. Without Jackson, Baltimore will likely lean on star running back Derrick Henry to help take the pressure off Fagnano. Henry remains one of the NFL's premier RBs. As long as he is on the field, the Ravens remain a dangerous team. Stopping Henry is number one of my five keys to a Jaguars' victory . Jacksonville has the league's top run defense, but it will be hard to overcome the loss of Hamilton. Expect the Jaguars to load the box to keep Henry contained and force Baltimore's crippled passing attack to beat them. Offensively, Jacksonville's potent attack should have success against a Ravens defense that allows over 25 points per game. QB Trevor Lawrence is playing at an MVP level and could have a big night against Baltimore's suspect pass defense. For the second game in a row, the Jaguars are playing a team that will be at much less than full strength. Last week, the Colts got an early start on their rebuild by trading stars Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner before playing Jacksonville. Now the Jaguars get to play a Ravens team missing its superstar QB and his primary backup. An undrafted rookie QB making his first NFL start against a terrific team like Jacksonville is a nightmare scenario for the Ravens. In the days of Ray Lewis, Ed Reed, and Terrell Suggs, Baltimore's defense could dominate a game without needing help from the offense. Those days are long gone. The Jaguars dominate and improve to 6-2. Prediction: Jaguars 34, Ravens 10

picks.blurb: Ravens Slammed With Horrific Prediction Hours Before Jaguars Game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football NFL Week 9 updates Luka has tight back Rivers to coach NC State CFB winners and losers Ravens Slammed With Horrific Prediction Hours Before Jaguars Game (Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images) Evan Massey · Roundtable Sports Thu, November 5, 2026 at 4:17 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Baltimore Ravens badly need to figure out how to come through with a win on Thursday Night Football to kick off Week 9 against the Jacksonville Jaguars. On the positive side, the Ravens will be playing in front of their home crowd. However, they are going to be playing without superstar quarterback Lamar Jackson and backup signal caller Tyler Huntley. Getting the start will be undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano. He came into the game last week against the Buffalo Bills and made his NFL debut, completing 10 of his 21 pass attempts for 91 yards, no touchdowns, and an interception. Hailing from Boston College, the 6-foot-3 and 225-pound quarterback threw for 3,448 yards, 28 touchdowns, and just one interception in 2025 with the Huskies. He completed 69 percent of his passes that year and chipped in with 131 yards and three touchdowns on the ground. Behind Fagnano, the team will have Kedon Slovis as the primary backup. He was signed off of the Green Bay Packers' practice squad this week. Baltimore has made the move to acquire Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals, but that trade will not finalize until later in the week. He won't be eligible to play against the Jaguars. Just hours before the game against Jacksonville kicks off, the Ravens have been slammed with a horrific prediction. Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio isn't giving Baltimore any chance to knock off the 5-2 Jaguars. He is predicting that the Ravens will be defeated by a final score of 27-13. At the end of the day, Baltimore has a lot of adversity to overcome. Sometimes, teams find the best of themselves in these moments. But, there is no question that the Ravens are facing an uphill battle against one of the top contenders in the AFC. Coming into this week's game, Baltimore has lost three straight games. Following their impressive 4-1 start, the Ravens are just 4-4 at this point in time. Obviously, the team's playoff hopes are very much in danger. Baltimore's hopes of winning a Super Bowl seem all but over. No one can fully count the Ravens out, but things are looking bleak. A win over Jacksonville would be a huge step towards getting back on track. On the other hand, a fourth straight loss would put Baltimore in a very difficult situation. Kickoff tonight is scheduled for 8:15 p.m. ET. Fans will be able to watch the game on Prime Video.

away.headline: 'No Excuses,' Ravens HC Reacts to Blowout Loss to Jaguars After Lamar Jackson Injury
away.blurb: With Jackson out due to a right thumb injury and backup quarterback Tyler Huntley sidelined with a toe injury, the Ravens turned to undrafted free agent Joe Fagnano under center. Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter wasn't interested in using the absence of star quarterback Lamar Jackson as an excuse for the team's 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday. "Obviously it's a tough situation for our guys," Minter told reporters after the game. "But, I just told them there's no excuses. There's no whatever, we don't have this guy, we don't have that guy. We've got to make a decision again over this break, got a little bit of a break for the guys to mentally reset and come back and seek improvement in all three phases. That's what we'll be after." Lamar's Message to Ravens 🎙️ Fagnano finished 10-of-18 for 60 yards and two interceptions against Jacksonville. "I'm not here to make excuses," Fagnano said after the game, per Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic. "We just didn't execute. I have to play better." He was appearing in the second game of his career, as he previously threw for 91 yards while getting picked off once during the Ravens' 36-10 defeat at the hands of the Buffalo Bills on Sunday. Baltimore's offense was only able to muster three points through three quarters against Jacksonville, finally finding the end zone with a 65-yard rushing touchdown by Justice Hill as the Jaguars held a 33-3 lead in the fourth. The Ravens picked up just 10 first downs while committing three turnovers during the contest. They averaged 4.2 yards per play. Baltimore has now lost four consecutive games since opening the season with a 4-1 record. The Ravens' struggles without Jackson have been particularly disappointing considering the two-time MVP started the year by completing 70.1 percent of his passes for 967 yards and six touchdowns compared to one interception. He also rushed for 144 yards and one score. away.headline: Jaguars-Ravens Injury Report: Why Recent History Doesn't Bode Well for Bhayshul Tuten
away.blurb: The Jaguars released their final injury report for Thursday's Week 9 battle with the Baltimore Ravens, and it featured two big names as questionable: running back Bhayshul Tuten and defensive end Travon Walker. There is understandable concern for both, with Walker limited in practice on Tuesday and Wednesday after sustaining a rib injury in last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts. But recent history under this Jaguars regime suggests Walker has at least a chance to play. It does not say the same about Tuten. Simply put, the Jaguars will more than likely need Chris Rodriguez Jr. to step into a starting role on Thursday based on how they have handled past injury situations. Tuten did not practice on Tuesday or Wednesday, despite Jaguars head coach Liam Coen indicating in his pre-practice press conference that Tuten would have some sort of practice activity. Instead, Tuten was a DNP for the second day in a row, which has resulted in a missed game each time during the Coen era. This is the 25th game where the Jaguars are led by Coen and his staff. In the previous 24 final injury reports, the Jaguars have had 27 instances where a player did not practice during the week. In all 27 of those instances, the player missed the game that week. The key difference here is that Tuten is at least listed as questionable. All 27 previous instances of players missing practice led to them being outright ruled out, which of course has not been the case with Tuten. Coen has already tabbed Tuten as a game-time decision, something he has done two other times this year: in Week 1 with Cole Van Lanen and LeQuint Allen, who were each listed as questionable but played. The difference is that Van Lanen and Allen at least practiced that week. If this was a full week and not a Thursday Night Game, which the Jaguars have not played under Coen before, perhaps things would be different. But for now, most signs point toward Tuten not being available just simply based on the Jaguars' history under Coen. Perhaps one key that could answer the Tuten question is how Coen approached Van Lanen's status in Week 1. Van Lanen was coming off a serious knee injury that had kept him out of the entirety of training camp, though he returned in time to be limited in practice in Week 1. home.headline: 'No Excuses,' Ravens HC Reacts to Blowout Loss to Jaguars After Lamar Jackson Injury
home.blurb: With Jackson out due to a right thumb injury and backup quarterback Tyler Huntley sidelined with a toe injury, the Ravens turned to undrafted free agent Joe Fagnano under center. Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter wasn't interested in using the absence of star quarterback Lamar Jackson as an excuse for the team's 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday. "Obviously it's a tough situation for our guys," Minter told reporters after the game. "But, I just told them there's no excuses. There's no whatever, we don't have this guy, we don't have that guy. We've got to make a decision again over this break, got a little bit of a break for the guys to mentally reset and come back and seek improvement in all three phases. That's what we'll be after." Lamar's Message to Ravens 🎙️ Fagnano finished 10-of-18 for 60 yards and two interceptions against Jacksonville. "I'm not here to make excuses," Fagnano said after the game, per Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic. "We just didn't execute. I have to play better." He was appearing in the second game of his career, as he previously threw for 91 yards while getting picked off once during the Ravens' 36-10 defeat at the hands of the Buffalo Bills on Sunday. Baltimore's offense was only able to muster three points through three quarters against Jacksonville, finally finding the end zone with a 65-yard rushing touchdown by Justice Hill as the Jaguars held a 33-3 lead in the fourth. The Ravens picked up just 10 first downs while committing three turnovers during the contest. They averaged 4.2 yards per play. Baltimore has now lost four consecutive games since opening the season with a 4-1 record. The Ravens' struggles without Jackson have been particularly disappointing considering the two-time MVP started the year by completing 70.1 percent of his passes for 967 yards and six touchdowns compared to one interception. He also rushed for 144 yards and one score. Baltimore will now look to bounce back in its next game, a matchup with the Los Angeles Chargers on Nov. 16. 00:37 Jeremiah Smith UPSET 🤬 TOP NEWS Bleacher Report • 7h Giants Pull JT Trade Offer Bleacher Report • 4h Week 10 CFB AP Top 25 Poll 🔢 Bleacher Report • 4h Mahomes Addresses Elbow Injury Postgame Bleacher Report • 2h Shedeur Solid Despite Browns Loss Live Updates Bleacher Report • 6h Live: Updates from every NFL game Bleacher Report • 1h Michigan Fires OC Bleacher Report • 4h Ja'Marr Shades Falcons CB 😏 Bleacher Report • 6h Browns Lose in OT Thriller 😞 Bleacher Report • 6h Knicks PG Sings Taylor Swift 😂 Bleacher Report • 3h J.J. home.headline: Lamar Jackson told Ravens he’s coming back this season, report says
home.blurb: Injured quarterback Lamar Jackson told teammates that he plans to return later this season, the NFL Network reported Sunday, citing anonymous sources. NFL Network reported that Jackson is undergoing surgery to repair a fractured and dislocated thumb on his right hand. Jackson’s injury typically takes at least six weeks to recover from, though it could take up to nine weeks, the report said. That would line up with a potential return during the Ravens’ four straight AFC North matchups to end the regular season, beginning Dec. 20 at the Pittsburgh Steelers. Perhaps the Ravens still have hope. “Just stay alive” was the paraphrase of Jackson’s message that he delivered within 24 hours of suffering a significant thumb injury on his throwing hand against Buffalo, the report said. After starting 4-1 with Jackson under center, Baltimore has slipped to 4-5 and last place in the AFC North, facing long odds to make the postseason. Jackson suffered the thumb injury on the offense’s first play of his first game back from an ankle injury in a 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Nov. 1. He and backup Tyler “Snoop” Huntley, who suffered a season-ending turf toe injury against Buffalo, were placed on injured reserve before Thursday night’s 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars , meaning they will miss at least four games. Jackson has not spoken to reporters since the injury, and coach Jesse Minter has declined to share details about it or Jackson’s potential recovery timeline. “I’m not going to speak on that,” Minter said when asked about Jackson on Thursday night. The Ravens have made plans to move forward without their two-time NFL Most Valuable Player this season, acquiring quarterback Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals last week. Though neither side disclosed the terms, Baltimore is reportedly sending Arizona a 2027 fourth-round draft pick and a 2028 seventh-round pick in exchange for the 33-year-old veteran and a 2027 fifth-round selection, ESPN reported. Brissett has started 73 of 109 games and completed 62.1% of his passes with 86 touchdowns and 39 interceptions. He also has 17 career rushing touchdowns. He is 23-50 as a starter. The move came about 12 hours after Baltimore’s embarrassing loss to the Jaguars at M&T Bank Stadium, where undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano made his first NFL start and struggled mightily with a heavily bandaged right ankle. He completed 10 of 18 passes for just 60 yards and was intercepted twice. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights The NFL returns to Spain for the second straight season with a matchup that features many of the league's top offensive stars Getty Images Following a week without an international game, the NFL heads back overseas in Week 9 when it sends the Atlanta Falcons and Cincinnati Bengals to Spain. The Bernabéu will play host to American football for the second time in as many years as two divisional contenders descend upon Madrid. The Bengals are in search of their first win away from American soil in franchise history after going 0-1-1 in their previous two opportunities (the most recent contest dating back to 2019), while the Falcons seek to improve to .500 in games abroad. Atlanta is 2-3 away from the United States and last season lost in Berlin. This contest pits one of the league's hottest teams against a squad that aims to reestablish positive momentum. Cincinnati rides a three-game win streak into the Madrid Game and scored no fewer than 31 points in any of those triumphs, albeit with two of the matchups coming against bottom-tier competition. Atlanta, on the other hand, lost in two of its last three outings and went scoreless in its most recent showing. Both sides are alive and well in their respective divisions, but the context between the two differs greatly. The Falcons are just a half game back of first place in the NFC South, which may be the weakest division in football with no teams at or above .500 through the season's first two months. The Bengals' position at half a game out of the AFC North lead is the superior standing considering three teams own winning records. Where to watch Falcons vs. Bengals live Date: Sunday, Nov. 8 | Time: 9:30 a.m. ET Location: Bernabéu (Madrid) TV: NFL Network, stream on fubo Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bengals -3, O/U 52.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook Falcons vs. Bengals key storylines Bijan Robinson and Drake London see bounce-back opportunity: It is no small feat to keep one of the NFL's top running back-wide receiver tandems in check, but how much credit do the Tampa Bay Buccaneers deserve for doing so in Week 8? With due respect to a formidable defense, the weather in that shutout might have had more to do with the Falcons going scoreless than anything else. A major one-week swing could be in store for this duo as it squares off against a Cincinnati unit that just allowed the Tennessee Titans to rack up 36 points. Robinson remains the league's rushing leader with 780 yards on the year, and London stands sixth in receiving yards at 624. If the Bengals could not keep the Titans in check, they will have their hands even more full with these two stars. Tee Higgins reaches new echelon: Higgins has long played second fiddle to Ja'Marr Chase in the otherworldly Bengals passing attack but is now on level ground with his superstar teammate. Both saw exactly 61 targets across their first seven games, and both grabbed 43 catches on those opportunities. But Higgins has been the far more efficient receiver of the two with 726 yards. That ranks second in the NFL, only to potential repeat Offensive Player of the Year winner Jaxon Smith-Njigba . This is the best version of Higgins the league has seen, and it is on pace for historic production . James Pearce Jr . to make season debut: The NFL reinstated Pearce after he served an eight-game suspension for a violation of the league's personal conduct policy, which makes him eligible to play for the first time this season in Week 9. Atlanta has been surprisingly disruptive on the defensive front without the second-year pass rusher, who faced felony charges this offseason following a domestic dispute but is on track to have those charges dropped. A unit that ranks sixth in quarterback pressure rate may climb even closer to the top of the leaderboard and perhaps improve its sack totals upon Pearce's insertion into the lineup, because he logged 10.5 sacks as a rookie despite starting only three games. Joe Burrow on MVP pace: Only two quarterbacks ( Josh Allen and Brock Purdy ) have shorter odds, via DraftKings Sportsbook, to win the NFL's top individual award. Burrow leads both of them in touchdowns with a league-best 20, and he is a mere 0.1 points away from the NFL lead in passer rating at 111.6. This is so far the most efficient season of Burrow's stellar career, which is a pleasant development of an offense that missed him dearly when he missed a combined 16 games over the last three seasons due to injuries. The Falcons kept Purdy in check when they upset him and the San Francisco 49ers two weeks ago, but Burrow presents an even greater challenge and has a healthier supporting cast than the one Purdy brought into the Week 7 contest. Falcons vs. Bengals prediction Fans of American football in Spain are in for a treat, because this game has all the makings of a shootout. There is not an offense in the NFL that is clicking quite like the Bengals over the last three weeks, and between Burrow, Chase, Higgins, London and Robinson, five of the biggest names in football will be in action in a star-studded battle. Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr . should bounce back from last week's dreadful 8-for-24 showing in the rain, so Atlanta ought to have enough juice to keep pace with a team that is averaging 36.3 points per game since Oct. 11. In a matchup where points will be aplenty, the team with the better defense holds the edge. It is not as though Atlanta is vastly superior on that side of the ball, but it is much more reliable and is about to insert one of its projected top producers into the lineup for the first time this season. There is not a more opportune time for a disruptive pass rusher like Pearce to make his first appearance than against arguably the best quarterback in the NFL. That alone could be the difference in a high-variance matchup like this one. With injuries beginning to catch up with the Falcons , slowing down Cincinnati’s passing attack could be a major challenge. Atlanta’s offense will also need to deliver a strong performance against a Bengals defense that has struggled at times this season. Michael Penix Jr. and Bijan Robinson will be important pieces as the Falcons attempt to keep pace with Burrow and company in what could be a high-scoring international matchup. Here are the Falcons On SI staff’s predictions for Sunday’s Week 9 matchup. Garrett Chapman (4-4) The Falcons will have a difficult test on Sunday with the high-flying Bengals offense. They will score plenty of points in this one, and it will be on Michael Penix Jr. to match that production. Working in their favor is the fact that the Bengals are not an elite pressure team, so if they can keep the quarterback clean, then the Falcons could keep up. International game, and the Bengals have been rolling with three-straight wins. This game could make for fireworks. Cincy is pretty much the middle of the pack defensively, but has one of the top offenses in the league. So the Falcons will have opportunities to put points on the board too. But can their secondary keep up with the likes of Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins? We have to wait and see if they prove it. Heading into Sunday’s matchup against the Bengals, I think Joe Burrow and Cincinnati’s offense will be too much to handle, especially with Atlanta’s injuries beginning to catch up with them. I expect the Falcons to keep it close, but ultimately, I’m taking the Bengals to win 27-24. While Cincinnati rides a three-game winning streak into this matchup behind Joe Burrow's red-hot play, our top Bengals vs. Falcons predictions and NFL picks examine whether the Falcons' feisty secondary can limit big plays, opening up prime betting edges on Tee Higgins as the Bengals look to extend their momentum across the pond. Here are my best bets and NFL picks ahead of Sunday, Nov. 8. Bengals vs Falcons prediction today: Falcons +3.5 The Cincinnati Bengals are rolling right now, but those victories have come against some weaker opponents. They took down bottom-feeders like Miami and Tennessee (barely), while needing a second-half rally to overcome Baltimore and a backup QB. There was also a bye in Week 6 giving Cincy a breather. I believe the Bengals should be the favorites in Spain, but not by this many points. The Atlanta Falcons are coming off a strange Week 8 loss in which weather played a huge role in the result. That included four interceptions from QB Michael Penix Jr. , who had only one INT in the previous five starts. I'm not discounting Atlanta too much for that rain-soaked squash at Tampa Bay. Rather, I see the Falcons facing one of the easier defenses on their recent schedule, with the Bengals stop unit slipping the past three games. The most notable dip has come defending the run. The Bengals are allowing 5.1 yards per carry in their last three outings (second most in the NFL). Not what you want to see when staring down Bijan Robinson . Bengals vs Falcons combo The Bengals should be favorites, but their current three-game win streak is very puffed up, and Atlanta poses a stiffer test on a neutral field. I'll take Atlanta on the other side of a field goal. Chase Brown hasn't found paydirt since Week 1. The Falcons have given up 11 total touchdowns to running backs and Brown is a dual-threat option, either running it past the goal line or catching a TD strike. Tee Higgins could be the best WR2 in the league. He's the top-rated WR versus man coverage and faces plenty of one-on-one coverage from Atlanta. Joe Burrow was slinging it against Tennessee last week, with five passing touchdowns. away.headline: Cowboys’ Jerry Jones Makes Clear NFL Trade Deadline Statement Amid Injuries
away.blurb: The Dallas Cowboys head into Sunday’s Week 9 game against the Colts in decidedly rough shape on both sides of the ball, with star receiver George Pickens and star cornerback Joey Porter Jr. both out, as well as starting linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, who had been playing better before injuries again caught up to him. The combination of those injuries and the looming NFL trade deadline has raised questions, again, about what Dallas might do in the next 48 hours ahead of that looming deadline. On the Cowboys’ pregame show on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas, owner Jerry Jones was asked by Kristy Scales whether the team will take this new wave of injuries into consideration at the deadline on Tuesday. “No,” he said, “but that doesn’t mean something could not happen. Actually, you almost have to say that if anything could be considered or working, you really don’t know until—if it is substantive, for sure—you don’t have any idea that it could happen until you have a meeting of the minds and it is done. But for now, I don’t see it.” Cowboys’ Jerry Jones Already Made an NFL Trade Deadline Move Indeed, the Cowboys are in a position in which a move at the NFL trade deadline might not make much sense, even if there is a win in Indianapolis that pushes this bunch to 4-5. If this group can’t beat the fire sale Colts, then obviously, there’s no point in adding at the deadline. But even with a win, the Cowboys are down to just four draft picks in the 2027 draft, and there just is not much more capital this team can afford to give away. Jones, who added Quinnen Williams in a blockbuster trade at last year’s deadline, has said that the move for Porter should be viewed as this year’s big deadline acquisition. Like HEAVY's content? Be sure to follow us . This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Cowboys’ Jerry Jones Makes Clear NFL Trade Deadline Statement Amid Injuries appeared first on HEAVY .

away.headline: Cowboys Breakout RB Leaves Week 9 vs. Colts Amid Injury Woes
away.blurb: Entering the Dallas Cowboys' Week 9 game against the Colts on Sunday in Indianapolis, there were already ample concerns on the injury front, as the team determined before kickoff that star receiver George Pickens and star cornerback Joey Porter Jr.–one of the defense's most important players–would be ruled out for the showdown. Those were tough blows, with the Cowboys essentially in a must-win game at 3-5 and hopeful of keeping alive their NFL playoff hopes. But during the game, more tough blows came, especially for running back Tyler Goodson, who has been settling into his role as the backup to Javonte Williams and who was eager to play the Colts, for whom he'd played his first three seasons after signing as an undrafted free agent from Iowa. Goodson was in the midst of his best game as a Cowboy on Sunday, taking seven carries for 44 yards, when he suffered a knee injury that left his return questionable. Backup running back has been an issue for the Cowboys going back to training camp, when the team had second-year men Jaydon Blue and Phil Mafah first in line for the job. Both players underwhelmed, though, and the Cowboys made veteran Malik Davis the backup. But Davis suffered a hip injury before the start of the year and was ruled out for the season. After a brief encounter with Emari Demercado , the Cowboys brought in Goodson, and appeared to be happy with him and the change of pace he brings behind Williams. away.blurb: The Thursday practice report out of Dallas contained optimism for Caleb Downs and P.J. Locke. Even though they remain in concussion protocol and the Cowboys admit they've looked at possible contingency plans for Sunday's game in Indianapolis, both starters were upgraded to limited and could be cleared to play Sunday. Unfortunately, that good news was tempered with some new situations to watch. DeMarvion Overshown is suddenly dealing with a hamstring/back issue, and Joey Porter Jr. got a slight downgrade as he continues to nurse an ankle. Over in Indianapolis, all eyes are on their potentially crowded trade block. Jonathan Taylor is reportedly getting a lot of attention (and it's become hard to ignore, he says), but the Colts likely won't make any deals until after the Cowboys come to town this Sunday. And Taylor may not be the only one. Josh Downs has said he wants out of Indy, and one NFL insider says even Daniel Jones may be on the move soon. (Answer: Longer than you probably think.) home.headline: Cowboys Breakout RB Leaves Week 9 vs. Colts Amid Injury Woes
home.blurb: Entering the Dallas Cowboys' Week 9 game against the Colts on Sunday in Indianapolis, there were already ample concerns on the injury front, as the team determined before kickoff that star receiver George Pickens and star cornerback Joey Porter Jr.–one of the defense's most important players–would be ruled out for the showdown. Those were tough blows, with the Cowboys essentially in a must-win game at 3-5 and hopeful of keeping alive their NFL playoff hopes. But during the game, more tough blows came, especially for running back Tyler Goodson, who has been settling into his role as the backup to Javonte Williams and who was eager to play the Colts, for whom he'd played his first three seasons after signing as an undrafted free agent from Iowa. Goodson was in the midst of his best game as a Cowboy on Sunday, taking seven carries for 44 yards, when he suffered a knee injury that left his return questionable. Backup running back has been an issue for the Cowboys going back to training camp, when the team had second-year men Jaydon Blue and Phil Mafah first in line for the job. Both players underwhelmed, though, and the Cowboys made veteran Malik Davis the backup. But Davis suffered a hip injury before the start of the year and was ruled out for the season. After a brief encounter with Emari Demercado , the Cowboys brought in Goodson, and appeared to be happy with him and the change of pace he brings behind Williams. Just because New York doesn't have the makings of a playoff contender doesn't mean it can't give Kansas City a fight, though. The Chiefs know as well as any team that self-inflicted errors are the easiest way to hand a game over, so the hosts will have to put the pedal to the metal in order to secure a resounding triumph. With kickoff just hours away, will it be the Chiefs or Jets that emerge with a victory? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 9 of the regular season. Joshua Brisco: While there's only so much the Chiefs can truly prove against the 2-6 Jets, this is a game Kansas City simply has to win. A two-game losing streak to a pair of playoff teams is one thing. A home loss to a franchise that’s still a year away from even making the “in the hunt” playoff graphic? That would be disastrous. I’ll be watching to see if the Chiefs’ pass rush can wrangle Geno Smith, who is tied for the second-most sacks taken among quarterbacks this season, while hoping to see more from rookie R Mason Thomas in that effort. Will the Chiefs’ banged-up defense be able to hold down a lively group of weapons, even without Garrett Wilson, or will the KC offense need to score more than 24 points for the first time since before the bye week? I could see a bounce-back stat line for Kenneth Walker with another explosive play or two from the star running back. Jordan Foote: The Chiefs typically have at least one game a year they have no business losing and somehow just don't seem to show up for. While it's possible that this is the one, it absolutely cannot be the case. Coming off ugly losses to the Seahawks and Broncos (for different reasons), this is a squad that desperately needs to rebound in a hurry. Fortunately, the matchup is there in Week 9. The Jets' offense has had its shining moments, although it's virtually impossible to trust this version of Smith to go toe-to-toe with Patrick Mahomes if he's on his game. Add in that Kenneth Walker III may be due for another statement performance, and it's hard to see anything other than turnovers or penalties making this too close of a game, in my view. Tyler Brown: The Jets have been more competitive than their 2-6 record suggests, with five of their six losses coming by one score, and Geno Smith has been a pleasant surprise. They can be dangerous on offense, with wideouts Omar Cooper Jr. and Adonai Mitchell playing well lately and running back Breece Hall returning, even as Braelon Allen's rushed for 565 yards. This is also a real test for tackles Kahlil Benson and Jaylon Moore, who will face pass rushers David Bailey and Will McDonald IV. On the other hand, New York’s defense has been giving up production to opposing tight ends, which sets up Travis Kelce and Noah Gray well. Andy Reid can wear the Jets down with Kenneth Walker and, in a perfect world, let Patrick Mahomes work the secondary off that. Smith is also among the league’s worst at turning pressure into sacks, so a Chiefs pass rush that's been waiting for a game like this should hypothetically get home a few times. Neither team will run away, and the Jets will stay in it for a while. But Kansas City is the more talented team and needs the win more. The Chiefs have a stretch of must-win games ahead, and they find a way to handle this one. Published 9 hours ago JORDAN FOOTE Jordan Foote covers the Kansas City Chiefs for Chiefs On SI. The two AFC opponents will meet on the gridiron for the first time since 2023 as KC returns to Arrowhead Stadium following a road stretch. Kansas City will be motivated on both sides of the ball after surrendering a double-digit lead in the fourth quarter to the Broncos. Now that the Chiefs no longer hold the lead in the AFC West, every game from here on out is crucial to staying alive in the division race. Meanwhile, the Jets are merely playing for draft position at this stage of the season, having lost six of their past seven matchups and presumably looking to sell a few key pieces at the trade deadline. However, head coach Aaron Glenn is also trying to preserve his job security and convince ownership he's the right man for the job. While sportsbooks favor the Chiefs in this one, what does the ESPN Matchup Predictor forecast? Here's what the computer model projects one day before kickoff. Dodson · Athlon Sports Fri, November 6, 2026 at 11:16 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs return home Sunday to face the New York Jets after dropping two straight games. Running back Kenneth Walker III has been bottled up in the defeats after leading the league in rushing through his first five games. The Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos limited K9 to a combined 105 rushing yards on 35 carries. Bold Prediction No. 1: Running Back Kenneth Walker Tops 100 Yards The Jets have allowed the seventh-most rushing yards to opposing running backs through eight weeks. Walker topped 100 yards on the ground in four of the first five games of the season. Even after averaging just 3.0 yards per carry the last two games, he's still second in the NFL with 5.5 yards per carry. Two weeks ago, the Jets allowed Miami Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon to rush for 103 yards on 25 carries . Walker is a clear upgrade from Gordon and will gash the Jets on the ground. The Chiefs' passing game has also had its issues. Tight end Travis Kelce has been managing an ankle injury, and they'll look to run the ball often. Bold Prediction No. 2: Chiefs Defense Records 2+ Sacks The Chiefs' pass rush has been much maligned, and it's for good reason. They're tied for last in the NFL with nine sacks on the season. Defensive tackle Chris Jones, who is one of their leading pass rushers, has just a half-sack on the season. Defensive end George Karlaftis reached the quarterback in Week 8 for his team-leading second sack of the season. The Jets are tied for second with 23 sacks allowed on the season. Quarterback Geno Smith has been sacked at least twice in the last seven games. Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo is known for his relentless blitzing, and the Chiefs will get home two or more times.

picks.headline: Previewing the New York Jets’ opposition: Kansas City Chiefs
picks.blurb: Previewing the New York Jets’ opposition: Kansas City Chiefs - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football NFL Week 9 updates Luka has tight back Rivers to coach NC State CFB winners and losers Previewing the New York Jets’ opposition: Kansas City Chiefs DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 1: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs runs with the football and looks to pass during the third quarter against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on November 1, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. The Broncos defeated the Chiefs 28-24. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bent Double · SB Nation Sat, November 7, 2026 at 4:00 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs have beaten the New York Jets in four of their five meetings since 2011, with the most recent being a controversial 23-20 win in 2023. That game saw Michael Carter II's game-clinching interception negated by a phantom penalty on Sauce Gardner and wasted one of the best performances of Zach Wilson's career. In this matchup, the Chiefs will be heavy favorites despite having lost two in a row following a 5-0 start. Let's break down the Chiefs' roster going position by position: The Jets have Patrick Mahomes to reckon with this week, and he's having a solid season as he's posting a quarterback rating of 99.7; his best since 2022. Mahomes has 12 touchdowns and four interceptions and is coming off a good game against the Broncos where he passed for 321 yards and three touchdowns with no interceptions. Behind Mahomes is a familiar face: Jets 2025 starter Justin Fields. Seventh round rookie Garrett Nussmeier is the number three. Offensive Line The Chiefs' interior line is the same as last year led by pro bowlers Creed Humphrey and Trey Smith at center and right guard respectively. Smith has a team-high five offensive penalties. Kingsley Suamataia completes the interior trio at left guard, although he's already been benched twice this year, including on Sunday where he was suddenly replaced before pre-game warmups by Mike Caliendo. That fuelled rumors that was was being disciplined by the coaching staff but Andy Reid denied this. Caliendo, who also started four games last year, has struggled in pass protection. Suamataia is expected to be back in the starting lineup for Sunday's game. The tackle positions have seen some changes as last year's starting right tackle, Jawaan Taylor, was released in March and the starting left tackle – 2025 first round pick Josh Simmons – is on injured reserve. Jaylon Moore, who started a handful of games last year, is currently starting at right tackle, while the left tackle is undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson, who is one of five undrafted rookies on the roster. Moore has given up a team-high three sacks, but Benson – while yet to surrender a sack – has given up the most pressure on the team. Moore missed week seven's game, so former New York Giant Joshua Ezeudu started at right tackle in that one. The other backups are center Hunter Nourzad and another undrafted rookie; tackle Diego Pounds. Running Backs The Chiefs' big offseason acquisition on offense was the reigning Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker. The move has been a resounding success as he rushed for 100 yards in four of his first five games as the Chiefs started 5-0. Since then, he's averaged just three yards per carry, though. Even so, he's just 10 yards off the league lead with 770 rushing yards. He has also caught 22 passes. There are two rookies backing up Walker – fifth round pick Emmett Johnson and the undrafted Jaydn Ott. Ott hasn't played yet, though. The Chiefs also have a fullback – Ben VanSumeren – on the roster. However, they will also use defensive tackle Khyiris Tonga in short yardage situations. He has even carried the ball twice. Pass catchers The Chiefs' top pass catching option has once again been tight end Travis Kelce, who has 410 receiving yards to lead the team. The leading pass catcher among the wide receivers is the speedy Xavier Worthy, who has 27 catches, albeit that he's only averaging 8.5 yards per catch. Despite some injury concerns and legal issues, Rashee Rice is now back in the lineup for the Chiefs. He has 20 catches in five games this year. Tyquan Thornton was also starting at wide receiver, but he's now on injured reserve. The backups are Jalen Royals, Andrew Armstrong, Nikko Remigio and fifth round rookie Cyrus Allen. Royals has seen the most action from this group. At tight end, Noah Gray is a solid contributor who gets plenty of playing time. Jake Briningstool and Jared Wiley round out this group. Defensive Line The Chiefs' defensive line is anchored by pro bowler Chris Jones, although he is having a down year statistically with just half a sack, one tackle for loss and three quarterback hits. He had 7.5, 12 and 25 last year. George Karlaftis, who had six sacks last year, has a team-high two sacks and also leads the team with 16 quarterback hits (just one less than the rest of the team combined) and six tackles for loss. Karlaftis also has a team-high with eight passes defensed. In fact, these all eight of these came in the last five games. Prior to that, he had 17 in his first 67 NFL games. Tonga is the other starter at defensive tackle with Felix Anudike-Uzomah the other starting defensive end. Kansas City has been operating a three-man rotation inside with first round rookie Peter Woods getting plenty of playing time. However, Woods has been ruled out with a neck injury so Bryson Eason may need to step up. Last year's second round pick Omarr Norman-Lott remains on the PUP list. The backups on the edge are second round rookie R Mason Thomas and Ashton Gillotte. Undrafted rookie Jack Pyburn is also on the roster. Nick Bolton remains in a full-time role with Drue Tranquill on the field most of the time. Last year, Bolton had 154 tackles and Tranquill added 103. They've been productive this year, too, with Bolton on 68 tackles and Tranquill on 53 tackles, including five tackles for loss. Jack Cochrane gets playing time in three-linebacker sets, while Jeffrey Bassa has seen limited action. Cooper McDonald has yet to play any defensive snaps, though. Defensive Backs The Chiefs suffered a loss a few weeks ago when their top cornerback L'Jairus Sneed was placed on injured reserve. Sneed was also the team's primary slot corner, so they've been using Christian Roland-Wallace in that role for the past few weeks. Nohl Williams and first round rookie Mansoor Delane are the current starters on the outside, although Kristian Fulton started in place of Delane on Sunday. Delane has a shoulder issue which is likely to limit him for the rest of the season but he was expected to return against the Jets. However, he has been ruled out, so Fulton will presumably start again. Melvin Smith and fourth round rookie Jadon Canady are also available to provide depth at cornerback. The starting safeties are Chamarri Conner, who had 117 tackles last season, and offseason signing Alohi Gilman. Jaden Hicks has also been getting playing time in three-safety sets. He also started the first three games with Conner out. Undrafted rookie safety Xavier Nwankpa has played five snaps so far this season. Special Teams Former pro bowl kicker Harrison Butker is having a rough year with six missed field goals already and Justin Tucker waiting in the wings on the practice squad in case he should falter again. Punter Matt Araiza is having his best year statistically in his third season with the Chiefs, though. Remigio is the team's return specialist, although Johnson ends up sharing the work on kickoff returns. Remigio, who is yet to achieve a 50-yard return as he is halfway through his third season, is officially listed as questionable. Bassa and Nwankpa are the team's most productive players in kick coverage this season, but last year they were led by McDonald and Cochrane. Canady and Nwankpa have been the primary gunners.

picks.headline: Chiefs-Jets Week 9 game and score predictions from Arrowhead Pride
picks.blurb: Chiefs-Jets Week 9 game and score predictions from Arrowhead Pride - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football NFL Week 9 updates Luka has tight back Rivers to coach NC State CFB winners and losers Chiefs-Jets Week 9 game and score predictions from Arrowhead Pride (Photo by Jim McIsaac/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jared Sapp · SB Nation Fri, November 6, 2026 at 6:30 PM UTC · 9 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to put their opinions to the test. Before the Kansas City Chiefs host the New York Jets — in their first matchup since 2023 — our writers predicted the final score and result. The 206 Jets are likely more focused on evaluating head coach Aaron Glenn — and the likelihood of having a trio of top ten selections in April's NFL Draft — than what happens the rest of the season. FanDuel Sportsbook currently lists the Chiefs as 9.5-point home favorites. Although the Jets lost to the Las Vegas Raiders 38-33 in Week 8, Gang Green did rack up 439 yards of offense, including 166 rushing yards. New York should not be considered a pushover opponent. We also want to know your score prediction! Vote in the poll on The Feed and share your score prediction ! Jared Sapp ( @TrumanChief ) It's been a hard fortnight to be a Chiefs fan. I am still of a mindset to see how this team looks at the end of the season, but losing any of the next three games would be catastrophic for the season. Earlier on, I was worried about the Chiefs sleeping on a team like the Jets. But after losing two straight games, I think the Chiefs will come out and play one of their best games of the season. The concern will remain of what happens against good teams, but I don't think you will see a play with their food performance at Arrowhead following a tough two-game road trip. Chiefs 31, Jets 17 Caleb James ( @CJScoobs ) After consecutive losses, the Chiefs badly need a win to get back on track. The Jets are a far cry from as bad as they have been in recent memory, but the Chiefs should win this game with minimal issues. The Jets are more talented offensively than they have been in some time, but running back Breece Hall has missed time this season with injury, and wide recieve Garret Wilson has shown up on the injury report. With a quality defense ranked near the top in several categories, the Chiefs will need to bring their A-game. Kansas City played a solid game offensively, but this week all eyes will be on the short-yardage and red zone situations where the team failed to convert in critical spots last week. Defensively, a turnaround game for the pass rush would be a big boost.I would continue to watch the emergence of Emmet Johnson alongside Kenneth Walker in creating a two-headed monster in the KC backfield. Chiefs 26, Jets 13 Mark Gunnels ( @MarkAGunnels ) I think the Chiefs are gonna handle the Jets at Arrowhead this week. If Garrett Wilson can't go, the Jets lose their best threat in the passing game, and Spags can load up on the run and make them beat Kansas City through the air. If Mahomes gets the Chiefs up two scores early, I don't see how the Jets keep up. I think this one gets out of hand in the second half. Maurice Elston ( @MrMauriceElston ) The Chiefs enter a three-game stretch that feels critical to keeping their AFC West title and No. 1 seed hopes within reach. After starting 5-0, Kansas City has dropped two straight, and the losing streak needs to stop Sunday against the Jets. New York has remained competitive, but this is a team the Chiefs should beat, especially back at Arrowhead in front of a crowd eager for something to celebrate. Garrett Wilson's uncertain availability could hurt the Jets, although Braelon Allen has proven their running game deserves respect regardless of Breece Hall's status. For Kansas City, getting Kenneth Walker III going starts with making defenses respect the passing game again. To me, his recent struggles go beyond the running back and offensive line. Tyquan Thornton's absence has taken away a deep threat, allowing defenses to crowd the line of scrimmage. The Chiefs must find ways to stretch the field without him, create room for Walker and get back to building off play-action. I expect Patrick Mahomes and Andy Reid to find those answers this week, with Kansas City settling down and delivering a convincing win. Chiefs 27, Jets 13 Matt Stagner ( @stagdsp ) The New York Jets come to town at a pretty good time for the Chiefs. Having lost the past two games, they'll be hungry to get back in the win column. Andy Reid has rightfully been blamed for the team's failures over the last couple of weeks, so I'd expect at least a "B" game plan on Sunday. He should let Kingsley come back as the left guard, and Rashee Rice is getting healthier— these two developments alone could get the offense moving enough to beat the Jets. But the Chiefs also have developing weapons in Emmett Johnson and Cyrus Allen. Both rookies should continue to see increased touches every week from here to the postseason (in my humble opinion). I'm of the opinion that the Chiefs are still in pretty good shape overall— the Denver loss hurt, but KC looked like the better squad. The Jets aren't as bad as their record either, so this won't be a cakewalk, but I expect the home crowd will have plenty to cheer about. Chiefs 28, Jets 13 Dakota Watson ( @D_Watson56 ) I hope the Chiefs are as angry as the fan base after that last game. Because they need to play angry, even against the Jets, if they're going to turn this season around. Now in a fight for the division, the Chiefs must take advantage of these next three games against what seems like inferior opponents. While I have serious concerns about this football team, I believe they get back in the win column this weekend. The offense should be able to get in a rhythm and right some of their wrongs from the past two weeks. And for the Jets, if Garrett Wilson can't go, then I think the Chiefs' defense should hold their own and focus on shutting down their running game. Chiefs win fairly comfortably in this one. Chiefs 28, Jets 17 Rocky Magana ( @RockyMagana ) It's been a rough couple of weeks. The Chiefs have lost back-to-back games. But they played well enough in Denver that they should have won that game. Some poor coaching decisions and a few mental lapses are all it takes in the NFL to lose to a division rival. That being said, this should be a get-right game for the Chiefs. The New York Jets are having a very Jets-like year and have struggled to move the ball and score points. They are also averaging 123.6 yards allowed per game on the ground. The Chiefs should plan on dealing a healthy dose of Kenneth Walker III and Emmett Johnson to them. This could be the perfect get-right game for Kansas City. Chiefs 24, Jets 10 Nate Christensen The Jets have been a better team this year. Their offense has dramatically improved with Geno Smith at quarterback and an impressive set of weapons. Braelon Allen has broken out at running back. Adonai Mitchell, Garrett Wilson, and Omar Cooper have formed a good trio. They have good young tight ends and two top-10 draft picks at tackle. Their offense can score and keep them in games The issue has been their defense, which is bad. They don't have a lot of talent, particularly in the secondary. I think the Chiefs should easily be able to throw the ball this week, and I expect Kenneth Walker to bounce back with a big game. Chiefs 34, Jets 23 Ron Kopp Jr. ( @RonOnChiefs ) Welcome to Game 1 of three that the Chiefs are fully expected to win, similar to the first five games of the season. The Jets are talented on offense and competitive on defense; they have too many recent first-round picks not to be, but there's nothing Aaron Glenn and company can do about Kansas City needing a confidence-building win after two straight losses. Look for the Chiefs' run game to come alive again and marry it to a passing attack that found answers against the Broncos last week until the final play. Whether the wide receivers are a big part of the game plan, I see Kansas City lighting up the scoreboard and putting this game out of reach in the second half. That will play a big factor in how we evaluate this backfield. I'm willing to chalk this up to being a poor game script and situation for both backs. The Jets offense struggled to move the ball and it was probably a gift Hall and Allen got to those fantasy totals. New York also wanted to work Hall back up to speed while also keeping Allen involved. WR Garrett Wilson (concussion) being out also doesn't help the unit overall. We may have to graduate the Broncos' backfield out of this series now that Coleman has taken things over. But we do have to see how the splits go once RB RJ Harvey is off injured reserve. Until then, it appears to be Coleman's job and Dobbins continues to fall further out of favor with head coach Sean Payton. Denver also has a great schedule down the stretch and one could assume Coleman, as a rookie, will only get better with more reps. home.headline: Patrick Mahomes injury update as Chiefs QB will have testing on elbow
home.blurb: "Obviously, I didn't feel great, but I was able to get it worked on, especially at halftime, and go out there and play the rest of the game." Mahomes grimaced in pain after a strip-sack by David Bailey, holding his right elbow as teammates helped him off the field. After being evaluated on the sideline, however, Mahomes went back to warming up and returned to play on the following series without missing a play. "If I'm able to play, I'm gonna play," Mahomes said in a news conference after the 35-12 win. "That's part of the game. That's part of playing. It scares you in moments when you get pains in certain areas of your body. On his first play back, Mahomes found tight-end Travis Kelce for a quick 12-yard connection, but kicker Harrison Butker missed a 51-yard field goal as time expired. Mahomes, who was sidelined for the remainder of last season by a torn anterior cruciate ligament suffered last December, drew a parallel to the knee injury, saying there was an initial "scary" element of uncertainty. He felt confident after throwing the ball on the sideline, however, that it not a ligament issue. Mahomes is set to undergo additional testing. He finished with 242 yards and two touchdowns on 23-of-31 passing. We may earn a commission when you buy through links on this page. home.headline: Chiefs reunion in doubt: Hill’s stalled recovery, civil verdict cloud NFL future; Kansas City weighs options
home.source: The Times of India on MSN
home.blurb: Tyreek Hill's injury recovery puts NFL return plans on hold The Chiefs could benefit from another proven receiver, particularly after injuries affected their available options. However, Hill is not the only name under consideration. Indianapolis Colts receiver Josh Downs has also emerged as a potential target. There is another issue the organisation must consider before bringing Hill back. In October 2026, a civil jury found him liable on two battery claims involving his estranged wife. The verdict adds to the questions surrounding his potential return. Tyreek Hill once made the Kansas City Chiefs' offence one of the most feared units in the NFL. Now, the possibility of seeing him back in a Chiefs uniform is becoming harder to imagine. The 32-year-old wide receiver is still waiting for his next opportunity after leaving the Miami Dolphins, but his recovery has not gone as smoothly as hoped. With Kansas City exploring other ways to strengthen its receiving corps, Hill faces a race against time to prove he can still compete at the highest level. His agent's cautious approach now looks increasingly justified. Get breaking news anytime, anywhere. Download the TOI app now! Miami eventually released Hill in February 2026, ending a chapter that began with his blockbuster arrival from Kansas City in 2022. His scheduled $51 million salary-cap hit also made his situation difficult for the Dolphins. Agent Drew Rosenhaus has maintained that Hill should not rush his recovery simply to secure another contract. That decision could prove important as teams assess whether the veteran can still deliver at his previous level. NFL reporter Pete Sweeney recently discussed Kansas City's interest during an appearance with Trey Wingo. He suggested the Chiefs could explore several options before making a decision. "I think the Chiefs will try to turn over every stone to try and get a quality receiver." However, Hill's physical condition remains a major concern. Sweeney also explained the timeline that had been discussed locally. "We had kind of heard locally that Tyreek Hill wouldn’t really be ready to pass a physical, take the field until early to mid November." Chiefs reunion faces competition and off-field concerns Sweeney acknowledged that Kansas City must weigh those concerns alongside Hill's football ability. "It's the type of player as well that it's ‘do we want to bring this player into the locker room?’ Just considering some of the off-the-field stuff, but at a certain point, the Chiefs showed us two weeks ago the off-the-field to them maybe doesn’t matter," Sweeney said. Hill finished his injury-shortened 2025 campaign with 21 catches, 265 receiving yards and one touchdown in four games. Until he proves his knee can withstand NFL demands, his comeback remains uncertain. A reunion with Mahomes and the Chiefs is still possible, but Kansas City has little reason to rush its decision. The Saints are coming off a much-needed bye week after a 2-5 start to the year. Meanwhile, the Browns are off to an unexpected 5-3 start but will be without starter Deshaun Watson . Here are our staff predictions. Grant Chachere , Lead Writer: W 24-10 This is a game I would have picked the Saints to lose, but things change. Cleveland quarterback Deshaun Watson is questionable for Sunday’s game, so the organization will start Shedeur Sanders . Because of this revelation, it 100% benefits the Saints. Watson has been one of the league's better quarterbacks all season. However, with him out for this game, the Browns’ offense is less of a threat, even with solid receiving options in wide receiver Denzel Boston and tight end Harold Fannin . Then, add to the fact that left tackle Kelvin Banks is back after missing significant time due to an ankle injury and rookie wide receiver and first-round pick Jordyn Tyson will finally make his debut after suffering a hamstring injury during fall camp, the Saints’ odds of winning only increase. This is a great opportunity for the Saints to get a win, especially with a three-game slate coming up. However, if the Saints don’t get a win, there will be a lot more questions than answers in New Orleans, especially for head coach Kellen Moore and the man who hired him, general manager Mickey Loomis . Saints 24 Browns 10 Doug Joubert , Publisher: L 28-17 The Saints made some moves after the bye week, firing their run game coordinator and bringing in a familiar face at kicker. I asked earlier this week in my column if it was a step in the right direction or window dressing. This week also carries with it the return of Kelvin Banks Jr. from injured reserve after limited practice opportunities Wednesday, Thursday and Friday. Add to that first-round pick Jordyn Tyson makes his debut in a Saints regular-season uniform this weekend. The surprise move for me was the timing of cutting 4th year running back Kendre Miller . Though I have been on the "get rid of Miller ASAP" train for a while, I did not expect it to happen the day before a game. These moves force me to look back at the first half of the season and wonder if this Saints team has gotten better as the year has worn on. The answer is no. The kicking game move to Charlie Smyth is a lateral move, maybe a little better. The return of Banks will be an improvement, but the Saints weren't doing all that well running the ball with him in the lineup before the injury. Replacing a run coordinator cuts down the amount of feedback you're getting as a coach about your rushing attack. That could be good and bad. The defense cannot stop the run, while the offense can't get it going. This is not a good team. Some want to blame Mickey Loomis, some Kellen Moore, some want to put the onus on the athletes that have been brought into the fold (or kept). I say all that to say this: Even with Shedeur Sanders starting at quarterback Sunday for the Browns, a definite step back from the usual starter Watson, this Saints team has quite a lot to prove before I can say with confidence that they can scratch out a win. I would love for this to be the game where the Caesars Superdome regains its reputation as a hell-hole for visiting teams. I would love to see Audric Estimé be the back who makes the difference (the way Saints fans would love him to be) instead of a guy who has bounced around from practice squad to practice squad his entire career. I would like to have Chase Young continue to hunt down opposing quarterbacks, and while he's at it to stop the run, too. And I'd love to see the Saints win Sunday. I just don't see it. Getting Kelvin Banks Jr. back along an O-line that has struggled to keep Shough clean in the pocket should also benefit Kellen Moore's unit. Sanders can smile all he wants, but the Saints will get the last laugh Sunday. picks.blurb: Final Prediction for Saints-Browns Week 9 Matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football NFL Week 9 updates Luka has tight back Rivers to coach NC State CFB winners and losers Final Prediction for Saints-Browns Week 9 Matchup Caleb Yaccarino · Roundtable Sports Sun, November 8, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads After two weeks without New Orleans Saints football, we are finally back. The Saints are also making their return to New Orleans, which may honestly be bad news for this team. The Saints have been unable to win a game at home this year, and some of their worst performances happened in New Orleans. For a team that has always valued the impact of playing at home, this is a really bad situation to be in, especially given how vocal fans can be. It also doesn't help that the pressure on the coaching staff to perform is palpable. The Saints also made some really important changes before this game. The Saints fired run game coordinator T.J. Paganetti, and they cut some players, including kicker Daniel Carlson and RB Kendre Miller. Each move made sense, and it is the first time we have seen real consequences from Kellen Moore's coaching staff. As I mentioned, the pressure is on this team, so we might as well try new things. For their opponent, it is a winnable game. The Cleveland Browns have been surprisingly one of the best teams in the NFL this season. They have had to make some crazy comebacks to make it happen, but QB Deshaun Watson is having a resurgence in his career. The defense is also playing really well, with the pass rush and pass defense standing out. But Watson is likely going to be out for this game. As of now, Watson has missed practice all week and is questionable for Sunday, so Shedeur Sanders will likely start for Cleveland. Although Sanders has not played yet this year, the Saints shouldn't overlook what the young QB can do. He had ups and downs throughout his rookie year, and if he is on point when facing the Saints' defense, it can be difficult to stop. The real worry for New Orleans is the Browns' defense. They have had run defense issues, so if the Saints defy all odds and fix the run game, that could be a way to win this game, but the rest of the defense will cause issues for the Saints. Now on to the prediction. Even with Watson likely being out, it's extremely difficult for me to choose the Saints. I do think it's going to be a close game, just not a victory for New Orleans. They need to prove the changes actually mattered first before I can believe something will change. For the score, I have the Browns winning 30-28.

away.headline: Cleveland Browns Practice Report for Wednesday November 4 Week 9
away.blurb: The Cleveland Browns wrapped up practice Wednesday at the CrossCountry Mortgage Campus in Berea, and there are nine players on the injury report. Quarterback Deshaun Watson, who took a helmet-to-helmet hit in the Week 8 game against the Pittsburgh, entered the concussion protocol this week. He did not practice on Wednesday. The Browns had a total of four players who did not practice in the first official session of the week, while five other players were listed as limited participants. No one on the practice report was able to take part in a full session. Browns defensive tackle Maliek Collins (elbow) left the Week 8 game against the Steelers due to an elbow injury. He suffered the injury in the second quarter, and he was considered questionable to return. And, return he did, as Collins made his way back into the game in the third quarter. He finished with four total stops and a tackle for loss in Pittsburgh. Also on defense, cornerback Myles Harden (hamstring), linebacker Carson Schwesinger (wrist, ankle) and defensive end Jared Verse (knee) were listed as limited participants. All three played Sunday, with Schwesinger leading the way with 10 total stops, including four solo tackles. Denzel Boston Listed as Limited Participant Rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston (calf), who has been playing through injury for the past couple of weeks, was limited due to that aforementioned calf. He hasn't missed any game time, and he had six receptions for 37 yards, while tying tight end Harold Fannin Jr. for the game high with 12 targets in Week 8. Rounding things out on offensive, rookie offensive tackle Austin Barber (calf) did not practice, while center/offensive guard Elgton Jenkins (knee) was a limited participant. His named has dotted the injury report for several weeks, but he has been able to fight through the nagging lower-body injury to play. home.headline: NFL: Returning Charlie Smyth helps New Orleans Saints to overtime victory
home.blurb: The Down native made a telling impact on his return to action after his release last August. Earlier this week the 25-year-old was dramatically recalled by head coach Kellen Moore after being retained on the practice squad . Charlie Smyth gets the nod to make sensational new Orleans Saints return skip to main content Your browser does not support Javascript. Please turn Javascript on to get the best experience from rte.ie News New Orleans Saints 23-22 Cleveland Browns Charlie Smyth kicked three field goals, including one effort from 48 yards, as the New Orleans Saints secured a 23-22 overtime victory over the Cleveland Browns at the Caesars Superdome. Smyth - who signed a three-year deal last December – made a crucial contribution as the Saints secured their first home win of the season to improve their record to 3-5. Smyth's 30-yard field goal was the opening score of the game, with the sides level 3-3 at half-time. A second successful kick left it 6-6 at the end of the third quarter, while his biggest kick of the game, from 48 yards, nudged the hosts ahead in the fourth quarter having earlier missed a longer-range effort from 52 yards. 48 YARDS CHARLIE SMYTH 💪🇮🇪 A third field goal for the Irishman gives the @Saints the lead! https://t.co/dkp2TXVvl8 Cleveland however struck back through quarterback Shedeur Sanders, connecting with KC Concepcion on a 64-yard touchdown pass for a 13-9 lead with 5:21 to play. Saints quarterback Tyler Shough led a 55-yard scoring drive, capped by a two-yard touchdown by running back Audric Estime to move ahead 16-13 with 53 seconds to play. There was still time for the Browns and a 51-yard Andre Szmyt field goal forced overtime. The winning score came on a 15-yard touchdown catch by tight end Juwan Johnson with 4:17 to play in overtime. The Browns responded with a 39-yard touchdown pass to tight end Harold Fannin Jr with a minute to play, but their two-point attempt failed, handing the Saints victory. © RTÉ 2026.
