LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Plus, the Dolphins stifle Jared Goff and the roaring Lions offense Michael Owens/Getty Images Anything can happen in the National Football League, and the kickoff to Week 9 of the 2026 season certainly solidified that idea. The Baltimore Ravens defense entered Week 9 on a 12-game streak of not allowing a 50-yard play, but they allowed two to the Jacksonville Jaguars in the first half of a 33-10 "Thursday Night Football" home defeat. It's also incredibly stunning that Ravens running back Derrick Henry has run for under 60 yards in four consecutive games. However, he did surpass Pro Football Hall of Famers LaDainian Tomlinson and Jerome Bettis for seventh on the all-time rushing list Thursday night. It's also a good thing Baltimore traded for veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett this week because the Ravens have now scored 14 or fewer points in four straight games for the first time in Ravens history. What other shocking events could happen during the rest of the NFL's Week 9 menu of games? Let's take a look at five bold predictions. Joe Milton-led Eagles upset first-place Giants The New York Giants (4-2-1) are 3.5-point road favorites at the Philadelphia Eagles (2-6), per DraftKings Sportsbook, marking the first time they are favored over the back-to-back NFC East champs since 2016. It makes sense: The Eagles have lost six in a row, and the Giants have gone three consecutive divisional games without a loss. However, the Eagles will snap their losing streak on Sunday behind new starting quarterback Joe Milton III . Milton, who was Dak Prescott's backup with the Dallas Cowboys since 2025, was scooped up off of the Cowboys' practice squad by Philadelphia. He will take his turn at the wheel of the Eagles' offense after Tanner McKee lost all three of his starts this season. Milton will bring big plays back to Philadelphia's offense. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer has compared Milton's arm strength to that of Brett Favre , whom he coached with the New York Jets in 2008. This preseason, Milton showed significant strides in the accuracy and touch departments in Dallas' three exhibition games in 2026. He completed 29 of his 43 passes (67.4%) for 378 yards, three passing touchdowns and no interceptions for a 118.2 passer rating. Milton will use the lessons he learned from Prescott to emerge victorious over a Giants team Prescott has dominated throughout the course of his career. Vikings sack Bills QB Josh Allen more than five times Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores YOLO defense leads the NFL in the following statistics: Scoring defense (13.3 points per game allowed) Red zone defense (25% red zone touchdown rate allowed) Goal-line defense (37.5% goal-line touchdown rate allowed) Completion percentage allowed (56.2%) Touchdown-to-interception ratio allowed (4-8) Sack rate (11%) QB pressure rate (46%) Blitz rate (73.6%, the highest by any team in the 21st century) They are bad news for any offense, but especially a Buffalo Bills offensive line that is allowing a 38% quarterback pressure rate, the 11th-highest in the league this season. Bills 2024 NFL MVP quarterback Josh Allen has a propensity for going haywire in primetime against the league's top defenses. In the Week 12 edition of "Thursday Night Football" at the Houston Texans last season, Allen absorbed a career-high eight sacks. Playing on the road in Minnesota on "Monday Night Football" in Week 9 against Flores' ferocious pass rush group could lead to a slightly similar disaster. The Vikings will sack Allen over five times, something that has happened to him just four times in his nine-season NFL career. Cowboys hold the Colts to under 20 points The Cowboys' (3-5) defense hasn't recovered from trading away All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons to the Green Bay Packers less than a month away from the start of the 2025 season. Dallas has allowed 29 points per game since 2025, making them the second-highest-scoring defense in the entire league. That figure is driven by the Cowboys allowing 20-plus points in 15 consecutive games, the longest active streak in the NFL. However, they will go on the road and hold the Indianapolis Colts (2-6) to under 20 points on Sunday. Indianapolis is fresh off a 42-7 defeat at the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 8, and they have scored 10 or fewer points in consecutive games for the first time since 2022. Facing a familiar face in Colts quarterback Daniel Jones , whose 68.7 passer rating is the worst in the league this season, the Cowboys will finally hold a team under 20 points for the first time since Week 11 of the 2025 season. Jets' Braelon Allen goes off against Chiefs New York appeared to suffer a major blow when Jets running back Breece Hall , whom the team extended on a three-year, $43.5 million contract this offseason, went down in Week 3 with a quadriceps injury. However, 2024 fourth-round pick Braelon Allen slid into the Jets starting running back spot and has balled out ever since. Allen's 504 rushing yards in the five games since Hall's injury are the second most in the entire NFL behind only Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving's 548. Despite the 5-2 Kansas City Chiefs allowing the eighth-fewest rushing yards per game (96.3) in the NFL this season, Allen will go off for over 100 once again to become the first Jet with five consecutive games with 100-plus scrimmage yards since running back Thomas Jones in 2008. Dolphins hold Lions QB Jared Goff to under 200 passing yards The Detroit Lions (5-2) are soaring this season, leading the NFL in total offense (395.4 total yards per game) and ranking third in scoring offense (29.0 points per game). Quarterback Jared Goff is at the center of that success. Goff is averaging 280.6 passing yards per game (third in the NFL) with 15 passing touchdowns (tied for fifth in the NFL) and just one interception. Goff is the fourth quarterback to have those numbers through the first seven games of a season, joining Tom Brady (2015 and 2016), Alex Smith (2017) and Patrick Mahomes (2019). Goff is also third in the NFL in EPA per dropback (0.25). However, the Miami Dolphins (1-6) will keep Goff relatively in check by holding him to under 200 yards passing. The only team to do that to Goff in 2026 is the Vikings, the NFL's No. 1 defense. However, the Dolphins will do it on the strength of 2024 first-round edge rusher Chop Robinson's efforts. Robinson leads the NFL in quarterback pressure rate (20.6%) this season (among those with at least 100 pass-rush snaps), and Robinson will get in Goff's face enough to throw him off his game. Jameis Winston came off the bench to lead a 14-play, 76-yard go-ahead third-quarter touchdown drive in the tense moments when it looked like the cursed Giants had lost a second starting quarterback to a significant injury, and those points held up Sunday in a 19-11 victory against the Eagles that featured otherwise putrid offense from both teams. The Rams are 4.5-point favorites on the spread (Rams -4.5), with the over/under set at 47.5. Los Angeles is a -225 moneyline favorite while Washington is a +188 underdog. Let's get into my Rams vs Commanders predictions for today's NFC clash. Rams vs Commanders pick: Commanders Moneyline (+190) My Rams vs. Commanders best bet is Washington moneyline, with the best price currently available at FanDuel. Rams vs Commanders Odds Rams vs Commanders Spread : Rams -4.5 (-110), Commanders +4.5 (-110) Rams vs Commanders Over/Under : 47.5 (-120o / +100u) Rams vs Commanders Moneyline : Rams -225, Commanders +188 Rams vs Commanders Preview This handicap is entirely a bet against the health of Matthew Stafford . Stafford looked horrendous last week. He was seen icing his shoulder on the sideline, and the film backed up the injury concerns. He posted the lowest average depth of target (aDOT) of his entire career. The ball was fluttering out of his hand, floating downfield with hardly any zip — and if your quarterback cannot physically drive the football, you are in major trouble. To make matters worse, the Rams are still without Davante Adams on the outside, and their defense lost starting cornerback Jaylen Watson for the season. One major positive for the Rams on the injury front is that Myles Garrett is expected to play in this game. The reigning Defensive Player of the Year has been sidelined since Week 1 after undergoing knee surgery. Commanders Preview The Commanders defense remains incredibly stout against the run, largely thanks to their Brian Flores-esque scheme. Although the Commanders' 2-4-1 record is far from impressive, they remain a dangerous team that can win on any given Sunday. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn is currently fighting for his job , and injuries have plagued the team throughout a disappointing season. Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels has missed several games this season after aggravating a previous arm injury, while several other key players have been sidelined for significant periods of time. While they are 2-4-1, the Commanders still have an opportunity to win the weak NFC East. The Commanders just won their second game of the season after defeating the Philadelphia Eagles and currently sit third in the division. This season, the Commanders are 17th in points per game and 26th in points allowed. They have also struggled on third down, converting just 32% of their attempts, while their defense has surrendered too many points. Although the Commanders have been one of the worst teams this season, they have found success running the ball. Led by their dual-threat quarterback, they average 127 rushing yards per game and protect the ball with only three turnovers. The Commanders' biggest weakness lies in their passing defense, which ranks 27th in the league, allowing 243 yards per game and an opponent passer rating of 100.6. The Rams' success largely depends on quarterback Matthew Stafford's ability to effectively move the ball. Stafford is reportedly dealing with soreness in his right arm. He left the locker room after the Chargers game with a bag of ice on his right elbow. This could be a big game for Puka Nacua . Held to only 80 yards in Week 9, Nacua might have over 100 receiving yards this week. The Rams should still find success running the ball, but the overall game will depend on Stafford's effectiveness passing the ball. In a must-win game for the Rams, this news comes at the worst time. Tight end Terrance Ferguson will also return to practice this week after sustaining an ankle sprain against the Denver Broncos in Week 3. away.headline: Myles Garrett Reacts to Return from Injury in Rams' Win to Jayden Daniels, Commanders
away.blurb: After being sidelined for the last seven weeks due to knee surgery, Los Angeles Rams star edge rusher Myles Garrett made his long-awaited return to the lineup on Sunday against the Washington Commanders. The Rams entered Sunday's game ranked near the bottom of the league with just 12 sacks, as they surely felt Garrett's absence. His return could help Los Angeles regain its footing on defense just in time for the playoff race. AP Photo/Stephanie Scarbrough NFL Garrett appeared to be in top form, recording three sacks and a forced fumble as the Rams earned a 20-13 victory to improve to 5-4. He's now the first Rams player to have three or more sacks in a single game since his teammate Aaron Donald in 2021. "Honestly, it means so g--damn much. This is the kind of adversity that I really haven't faced in my pro career," Garrett told Fox Sports' Jennifer Hale after the game. Garrett Expected to Play Sunday Report: Puka to Undergo MRI on Knee Garrett also told reporters after the game that he felt a sense of relief to produce the way he did on Sunday. "It was a weight off my shoulders, just getting back to where I am," he said. "I'm nowhere near where I want to be as far as, like, my performance and things I know I can do and how I can move, but this is a confidence booster for sure." After a quiet start to the game, Garrett made his presence felt in the second quarter when he got to Commanders star quarterback Jayden Daniels and knocked the ball loose for the strip-sack. Omar Speights recovered the fumble, giving the Rams a chance for a field goal before halftime. Garrett then recorded his second sack early in the fourth quarter to help preserve Los Angeles' lead. Garrett got to Daniels for the third time on a late third down to end Washington's comeback attempt. Avila was hurt on a Kyren Williams run with 10:32 left in the second. Facing a first-and-10 from the Rams’ 20-yard line, Williams ran up the middle from the shotgun for a 4-yard gain, where he was tackled by a Commanders defender. Avila was injured during the run. home.headline: Commanders vs. Rams Friday injury report: Treylon Burks, Dyami Brown out
home.blurb: The Commanders receiver corps is being thinned out by injury. Washington will play Sunday’s game against the L.A. Rams without Treylon Burks or Dyami Brown, the team announced Friday evening on its official injury report. Burks is dealing with a foot injury that kept him out of practice all week. Brown suffered a calf injury in Thursday’s practice that the Commanders are concerned about. Johnny Newton was considered questionable on the injury report, as those on IR with open practice windows usually are. We should learn about his availability on Saturday. TE John Bates – Limited all week with a shoulder injury All this comes shortly after Terry McLaurin was lost for the year with a torn petellar tendon in his knee. As The Athletic’s Nicki Jhabvala originally pointed, Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams were the only receivers at practice who have caught a pass in a game to this point. That’s, well, not great. The injury report was relatively clean outside of that, though the team has absorbed significant recent losses of those — like Javon Kinlaw and Jeremy McNichols — who are now on injured reserve. Also, NFL Network reports that superstar Rams edge rusher Myles Garrett is expected to be activated off injured reserve for Sunday’s game. Here’s the full Commanders injury report: WR Dyami Brown – Suffered calf injury during Thursday’s practice WR Treylon Burks – Suffered foot injury vs 49ers DT Jer’Zhan Newton – 21-day practice window opened; returning from IR (pec) DL Shy Tuttle – Has a shoulder issue from Week 8 G Sam Cosmi – Dealing with a new knee injury, full practice Friday OT Josh Conerly – Dealing with a new finger issue QB Jayden Daniels – Still listed with Week 2 elbow dislocation TE Colson Yankoff – New knee injury What’s your level of concern with the state of the Commanders injury situation? The 3-4 Carolina Panthers may seem like just another sub-.500 opponent, but they can be dangerous. The Broncos must guard against the "trap-game" nature of this matchup and handle the Panthers on the road. It's an East Coast road game with an early start, which has traditionally been an obstacle for the Broncos, but not since Sean Payton became the head coach in 2023. The Broncos have turned that particular ship around. The Panthers have some young playmakers on offense and a defense that's better than some people realize. Nix has his best statistical game of the year, with 280 passing yards and three touchdown passes. away.headline: Broncos' Week 9 injury report: S Brandon Jones trending toward inactive
away.blurb: Denver Broncos starting safety Brandon Jones was among three players who missed practice for a second consecutive day and now appear highly questionable to play in Week 9 against the Carolina Panthers. Jones suffered a hamstring injury in last week's victory over the Chiefs and has yet to resume practicing. Ditto for defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike, whose shoulder issue has held him out. Ditto for cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine, who's dealing with an ankle affliction. Each player will need to get in at least a limited session Friday to have any chance of suiting up at Carolina. In more fortunate news, Denver's other starting safety, Talanoa Hufanga, was upgraded from DNP (Did Not Practice) to a limited participant on Thursday, giving him a shot at returning after being sidelined for the last three games with his own ankle malady. WRs Jaylen Waddle (chest) and Pat Bryant (ankle) were full participants, as well. Bryant will return from a four-game absence due to an ankle injury. On Carolina's side, five players did not practice: OLBs Jaelan Phillips and Trevis Gipson, CB Will Lee, OG Damien Lewis, and LB Bobby Okereke. Quarterback Bryce Young (ankle) was a full participant and will play against the Broncos. Assuming Jones is ruled out, Taylor Rapp would likely fill in as a starting safety at Carolina. If Hufanga can't go, Devon Key or JL Skinner would slot in next to Rapp. Skinner, in particular, had a standout game in last week's comeback victory over the Chiefs . Assuming Abrams-Draine is out of commission, second-year CB Jahdae Barron could see an uptick in snaps behind CBs Patrick Surtain II, Riley Moss, and Ja'Quan McMillian. Wide receiver Courtland Sutton and defensive end Zach Allen were also upgraded to full following a veteran rest day on Wednesday. Both will be active in Week 9. “You’ve definitely seen his ascension, and he’s very comfortable with what they’re doing," Broncos head coach Sean Payton said of Young on Wednesday. "It’s an explosive team. I think they’re seventh or eighth in explosives. They do a great job mixing the play action, the ‘RPO’ (Run-Pass Option) game. They’ve drafted well. So all those numbers are different today than they were two years ago.” Assuming Uwazurike is scratched, Sai'vion Jones would likely be penciled in as a starting DE opposite Allen, with third-round rookie DL Tyler Onyedim a possibility to make his NFL debut. Jones suffered a hamstring injury in last week's victory over the Chiefs and has yet to resume practicing. Ditto for defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike, whose shoulder issue has held him out. Ditto for cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine, who's dealing with an ankle affliction. Each player will need to get in at least a limited session Friday to have any chance of suiting up at Carolina. In more fortunate news, Denver's other starting safety, Talanoa Hufanga, was upgraded from DNP (Did Not Practice) to a limited participant on Thursday, giving him a shot at returning after being sidelined for the last three games with his own ankle malady. WRs Jaylen Waddle (chest) and Pat Bryant (ankle) were full participants, as well. Bryant will return from a four-game absence due to an ankle injury. On Carolina's side, five players did not practice: OLBs Jaelan Phillips and Trevis Gipson, CB Will Lee, OG Damien Lewis, and LB Bobby Okereke. Quarterback Bryce Young (ankle) was a full participant and will play against the Broncos. Assuming Jones is ruled out, Taylor Rapp would likely fill in as a starting safety at Carolina. If Hufanga can't go, Devon Key or JL Skinner would slot in next to Rapp. Skinner, in particular, had a standout game in last week's comeback victory over the Chiefs . Assuming Abrams-Draine is out of commission, second-year CB Jahdae Barron could see an uptick in snaps behind CBs Patrick Surtain II, Riley Moss, and Ja'Quan McMillian. Broncos' Week 9 Injury Report: Concerning Brandon Jones Update Skip to main content SI.COM Wide receiver Courtland Sutton and defensive end Zach Allen were also upgraded to full following a veteran rest day on Wednesday. Both will be active in Week 9. “You’ve definitely seen his ascension, and he’s very comfortable with what they’re doing," Broncos head coach Sean Payton said of Young on Wednesday. "It’s an explosive team. I think they’re seventh or eighth in explosives. They do a great job mixing the play action, the ‘RPO’ (Run-Pass Option) game. They’ve drafted well. So all those numbers are different today than they were two years ago.” Nov 1, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Denver Broncos safety Brandon Jones (22) makes a tackle on Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice (4) during the second quarter at Empower Field at Mile High. home.headline: Panthers DB Faces NFL Punishment for Controversial Hit and Jaylen Waddle Injury
home.blurb: Carolina Panthers cornerback Marco Wilson is a strong candidate for an NFL fine after taunting Denver Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle on Sunday. The hit that sent Waddle out for a concussion evaluation could draw a separate fine for Panthers safety Zakee Wheatley. The NFL and NFLPA singled out hits on defenseless players as one of five safety violations under a tougher repeat-offense policy this season. Three qualifying violations in a season trigger a one-game suspension. The league typically publishes its weekly fines the following Saturday. Wilson's flag is already on the record. The Week 9 report will show whether the league also takes action on the hit that sent Waddle out of the game. Panthers DB Faces NFL Punishment for Controversial Hit and Jaylen Waddle Injury - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Panthers DB Faces NFL Punishment for Controversial Hit and Jaylen Waddle Injury The Broncos raised eyebrows about Jaylen Waddle. Getty Erik C. Anderson · HEAVY Sun, November 8, 2026 at 10:20 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The distinction is in what the officials called. Wilson drew the taunting flag for what he did after the hit. Wheatley delivered the contact that left Waddle down and then being evalutated for a concussion, and officials did not flag the hit itself. The flag gives the league a clear basis to review Wilson for unsportsmanlike conduct. The NFL's published fine schedule lists $11,941 for a first taunting offense and $17,911 for a second. The league can adjust those amounts. Earlier this season, it fined Dallas running back Javonte Williams $11,941 for taunting and Chicago receiver Jahdae Walker $5,620 for the same violation, according to the league's accountability report. Jaylen Waddle Injury: WR Being Evaluated For a Concussion After Controversial Hit Denver Post columnist Troy Renck reported that Waddle was being evaluated for a concussion after taking the hit in the second quarter. Renck took issue with the contact to Waddle's head and the lack of a flag on the hit. Waddle had left the game with Denver up 10-0. Waddle had already given Bo Nix one of Denver's biggest gains of the first quarter. He caught a pass for 23 yards to move the Broncos across midfield on the drive that ended with Courtland Sutton's touchdown. Denver had listed Waddle with a chest injury during the week, but he practiced in full Friday and went into Sunday without an injury designation. The second-quarter hit brought a new concern for a receiver who had scored his second touchdown as a Bronco the previous week against Kansas City. Why the NFL Can Still Fine Zakee Wheatley for the Hit The NFL rulebook gives a receiver attempting to catch a pass defenseless-player protection. home.blurb: The Denver Broncos got a bit of a boost to start practice this week with wide receiver Pat Bryant being designated to return from injured reserve . He could play as early as this Sunday and was a full participant. There are several players who were held out today: Kris Abrams Draine, Talanoa Hufanga, Brandon Jones, and Eyioma Uwazurike were all non-participants. The biggest concern there is that Denver could be down both starting safeties in this game against the Carolina Panthers. While the reserve players had a fantastic game against the Kansas City Chiefs last week, it is always a concern when your best players are not out there each week. Given Hufanga's situation, I would guess they keep him out this game and just plan to have him make his return after the bye week. Pictured: C.J. Stroud, Justin Herbert. John Lanfranca · Action Network Sun, November 8, 2026 at 8:00 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Houston Texans (2-5) and Los Angeles Chargers (0-7) will face off today in NFL Week 9. Kickoff is set for 4:05 p.m. ET from SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, Calif. The game will broadcast live on CBS. The Texans are 5.5-point favorites on the spread, with the over/under set at 40.5. The Texans are -245 favorites on the moneyline while the Chargers are +200 underdogs. Let's get into my Texans vs Chargers predictions for Sunday, November 8. Texans vs Chargers pick: Chargers +6 My Texans vs Chargers best bet is on Los Angeles to cover the spread, with the best price currently available at DraftKings. Make sure to find the best odds by checking our live NFL odds page. Texans vs Chargers Odds Texans vs Chargers Spread : Texans -5.5, Chargers +5.5 Texans vs Chargers Total : 40.5 Texans vs Chargers Moneyline : Texans -245, Chargers +200 Texans vs Chargers Preview The Texans should not be six-point favorites on the road, even against a wildly disappointing Chargers team that is winless entering Week 9. The Chargers offense may be the most disappointing unit in football given their expectations heading into this season, but the Texans defense is not far behind. Houston ranks 19th in expected points added (EPA) per dropback and it simply cannot limit explosive plays through the air. The Texans have allowed 29 completions of 20 or more yards and 51 completions of 15 or more yards — both rank in the bottom three out of all defensive units. Just two weeks ago, J.J. McCarthy shredded Texans secondary. McCarthy attempted 12 passes that traveled 10 yards past the line of scrimmage — he completed seven of those passes for 196 yards for an average of 16.2 yards per attempt. The Chargers have not covered the spread this season. Backing a team that knows its season is over may seem like a futile effort, but there are a few interesting numbers that lead me to believe the Chargers will remain competitive and potentially earn their first victory of the season. Let's begin with several trends favoring the underdog: Using all of the data available in BetLabs, all underdogs in the month of November playing against teams with a winning percentage of less than 30% (like Houston) are 72-54-6, covering at a 57.1% rate. Filtering out the first two months of the season eliminates the potentially small sample sizes of teams that just got off to a slow start. In games played in November or later, when those underdogs are +6 or greater, they have covered at a 66.7% rate, going 24-12-1 against the number. This exact scenario has not occurred during the 2026 season, but since 2010, these underdogs are a remarkable 18-3 ATS, covering at a 85.7% rate. Since 2020, there have been 10 instances of such a circumstance — the underdog has covered in nine of those games. Honing in on very bad teams — teams with a winning percentage of 30% or less, playing as a home underdog of 6 points or more are 47-31-1 ATS, covering at a 60.1% clip in games played in November or later. The Chargers offense is averaging a league-low 1.2 points per drive this season. However, they showed signs of life last week as left tackle Joe Alt returned from injury. Justin Herbert averaged 8.0 yards per pass attempt — in fact, in games that Alt has started and finished, Herbert has averaged 7.3 yards per attempt. For context, that mark would be higher than what Dak Prescott , Matthew Stafford , Bryce Young and Jordan Love have produced this season on a per-pass-attempt basis. We can clearly evaluate that the Chargers defense is playing at a much higher level than what Houston has offered. Los Angeles is 10th in defensive success rate and eighth in EPA/dropback. Against a Texans team that cannot run the ball consistently (26th in EPA per rush), slowing down C.J. Stroud and the passing attack of the Texans is really the only concern of defensive coordinator Chris O'Leary. Furthermore, the Chargers have been excellent at getting off of the field on third downs in recent games. Over their past four games, they have allowed just 10 third-down conversions on 45 plays, boasting a league-best 22% conversion rate. Texans vs Chargers Week 9 Prediction, Betting Analysis It may feel uneasy to pull the trigger on backing a winless team, but this is a good opportunity to buy the Chargers at their absolute floor. Most importantly, you can simultaneously fade a team in the Texans that isn't particularly formidable on either side of the ball. Points will be at a premium in this game — as the total sits at 40.5 — meaning the six points we'll get gains additional value. My recommendation is to shop around diligently or to remain patient to secure a +6. It is unlikely this line moves in the direction of the Chargers as 65% of all the public tickets are backing the Texans. With that said, I'd play this down to +5 as the Chargers should push for their first victory in 2026/ Pick: Chargers +6 Texans vs Chargers Trends Texans vs Chargers Inactives Texans S Reed Blankenship TE Cade Stover RB David Montgomery G Febechi Nwaiwu T Braden Smith T Nate Thomas Chargers S Kendall Williamson DB Deane Leonard G Kayode Awosika WR Theo Wease WR Brenen Thompson Texans vs Chargers Weather

(Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jeremy Brener · SB Nation Mon, November 2, 2026 at 5:31 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-7 after falling to the Los Angeles Rams on the road in Week 8. Now the Chargers will have a chance to face off against the Houston Texans at home in Week 9. The Texans have found their fair share of struggles this season at 2-5, but they are fresh off of their annual bye and are well-rested for the matchup. The Bolts entered this week as 4.5-point underdogs, per FanDuel Sportsbook . The over/under is currently set at 41.5 points. The Chargers struggled once again when facing the Rams. The Chargers had a 9-3 lead with 2 minutes to go in the second quarter, but they proceeded to give up a touchdown drive to close out the first half, which gave the Rams the lead going into the locker room. From there, the Rams capitalized and scored twice more in the third quarter to take a 24-9 lead, which ended up being the final score. Hope is not lost for the Chargers as they hold on to the No. 1 overall pick for the 2027 NFL Draft. However, getting a win or two would give them some morale for the second half of the season. Perhaps this will be the week the Chargers will have a chance to get their first win. BFTB community, how do you feel about the Chargers possibly getting their first win of the season against the Texans at SoFi Stadium in Week 9? Let us know in the comments section below.

picks.headline: Chargers vs. Texans: 4 bold predictions for Week 9 matchup
picks.blurb: Chargers vs. Texans: 4 bold predictions for Week 9 matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football NFL Week 9 updates Luka has tight back Rivers to coach NC State CFB winners and losers Chargers vs. Texans: 4 bold predictions for Week 9 matchup Ricardo Sandoval , Chargers Wire · Chargers Wire Sun, November 8, 2026 at 2:22 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Chargers will do all they can to win their first game of the 2026 season. Los Angeles remains the only winless team in the NFL. They are certainly one of the league's more disappointing teams, and the Texans are in the same boat. The Chargers (0-7) will host the Texans (2-5) this Sunday. The two teams are nowhere near where they expected to be, but they'll hope this week helps one of them turn the tide. Here are four bold predictions for Week 9. J ustin Herbert throws for 300+ yards and one touchdown Herbert is coming off a season-high 257 passing yards. The 28-year-old completed 24 of 32 passes, another season-high. Although he recorded two interceptions, Herbert showed clear signs of improvement. Houston's defense allows 244 passing yards per game, the fifth-most in the NFL, which helps Herbert build on his Week 8 performance. Chargers force C.J. Stroud into two t urnovers The Chargers' defense is far and away their best unit of the three. I expect them to wreak some havoc on Stroud, although he has taken exceptional care of the football. Stroud has 11 touchdowns to just one interception and no fumbles. However, I'm predicting the Texans quarterback has at least one interception and a forced fumble. Chargers running backs combine for 100+ rushing yards The Chargers offense hasn't rushed for 75+ in their last two games. Los Angeles rushed for 64 yards against the Rams, averaging 2.6 yards per carry. Omarion Hampton could see an increased role in the backfield, with a fierce pass rush led by Will Anderson and Danielle Hunter. The Texans' rush defense is allowing 3.8 yards per carry (9th) and 98.0 yards per game (11th). While the Chargers' rush offense hasn't been what we expected, I think they'll find a better groove in Week 9, despite their opponent. Chargers score two touchdowns After going 27 consecutive offensive drives without scoring a touchdown, the Chargers will get in the end zone, not once, but twice. One of those touchdowns will come through the air, while the other will be on the ground. home.headline: Chargers final injury report before NFL trade deadline
home.blurb: The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-7 and continue to shock the NFL world by showing an unwillingness to trade any of their players despite facing down a lost season in 2026. Los Angeles had hoped to right the ship and gain some momentum coming out of their week seven bye but looked listless against the Los Angeles Rams in week eight. The Chargers do have other players who may be targets on the trade market but so far the word that has been put out to insiders around the NFL is that the Chargers are continuing to execute their plan of standing pat and trying to right the ship before heading into the 2027 season. The return of Donte Jackson to field is intriguing as he has been floated as a possible trade candidate and the Chargers have built up significant young depth both on the roster and the practice squad. The Chargers have been battered by injuries this season. The joke around the NFL may be about the San Francisco 49ers electrical substation and its proximity to the practice facility but someone may need to look into the water in Los Angeles with the amount of injuries both LA teams have faced this season. By week six, the Chargers had over half of their original 53-man roster either on that week's injury report or on injured reserve. The Chargers are already down to their fifth option at left guard and despite hope for getting reinforcements to face the Houston Texans, it appears guard Kayode Awosika, who has not played since week two, is still at least one week away from returning to the field. The Chargers opened the practice windows for tight end David Njoku and linebacker Denzel Perryman this week but it appears that neither are ready to be activated off of injured reserve just yet. The Chargers are set to get some depth at cornerback returning to the field with Donte Jackson and rookie Rodney Shelley clear of the injury report and will carry no injury designation into the game on Sunday. The Chargers front office has been shockingly unwilling to engage with trade calls despite their record generating buzz and demand . The most obvious trade candidate, edge rusher Khalil Mack, has publicly stated that he wants to stay and head coach Jim Harbaugh has echoed that sentiment at the podium. Whether Mack is simply being a consummate professional or he really does not want to uproot and leave his family behind remains to be seen with the trade deadline just days away. If the Chargers lose to the Texans, drop to 0-8 and maintain they are not willing to trade anyone, they might no longer be operating under logic and may be relying on the force. Los Angeles is starting to get some of their injured players back and perhaps, the front office and ownership feel getting the team somewhat stable during the back half of the season and heading into the offseason is more important than a few day three draft picks. It’s not who you play but when you play them. The Green Bay Packers will face the New England Patriots on Sunday. It’s a measuring-stick game for the Packers, who believe they are Super Bowl contenders. The Patriots played in the Super Bowl last year and believe they have the goods to take the next step. With a top-tier quarterback and coach and a strong defense, they will be a formidable challenge. The Patriots, however, will play without their top two receivers, A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs. Their premier tight end, Hunter Henry, is questionable with a foot injury that held him out of practice to start the week. Their starting guards, Alijah Vera-Tucker and Mike Onwenu, are on injured reserve. So is their top pass rusher, Harold Landry. Can the Packers take advantage of the “when you play them” part of that adage? Here are our weekly game predictions. Bill Huber’s Packers-Patriots Prediction The Packers have had some good fortune this season. They faced the Buccaneers without Baker Mayfield and the Bears without Caleb Williams. They will have more good fortune against the Patriots. While Drake Maye, last year’s MVP runner-up, will be the starting quarterback, he’s going to be playing with an incredibly shorthanded group of receivers. Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas and Kyle Williams are not the same as A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs. Good quarterbacks can make it work with whoever, so this won’t be a layup victory for Jonathan Gannon’s defense. However, New England’s pass protection has been leaky, with Maye facing the fourth-highest pressure rate in the league. Can the Patriots’ receivers get open before the Packers’ pass rush arrives on the scene? Added together, the game has been put on a silver platter for Green Bay’s defense to be the most powerful unit on the field. On the other side of the ball, it’s going to be a challenging day for Jordan Love, as well. The Packers, of course, can’t run the football, and it’s having an impact on the passing game with the play-action attack having become irrelevant . If the Packers can’t run the ball – and what reason is there to believe they will? – they’re going to have to deal with the teeth of the Patriots’ strong pass rush, which ranks fifth in sack percentage. Elijah Ponder – the best pass rusher that nobody has ever heard of – is seventh in the league with six sacks. With 3.5 sacks, Christian Barmore powers the interior rush. “He’s a really good player,” Packers coach Matt LaFleur said of Ponder, an undrafted free agent last year. “To be truthful, I hadn’t heard a whole lot about him until I started watching the tape and I’m like who is this guy? What’s his story? How do we not know about him? Everybody knows about him now. When you look at their edges, all three of those guys that are really doing the bulk of the work are really good players, and you couple that with the interior guys, it’s a really formidable front.” That could mean limited time for Christian Watson and Matthew Golden to beat the premier cornerback duo of Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis. “Really good DBs,” Love said. “I think they do a lot of things very well. I think as anything, it’s a challenge for me, for the receivers on the outside to be able to go see how good we can be and how good we can attack them and make plays against them. I think they do a really good job. I think Gonzalez is definitely one of the best in the league and he makes plays. I feel like for us, it’s a fun test.” Ultimately, I’m taking the Packers, who are 3-point underdogs at FanDuel Sportsbook . Both quarterbacks are really good, but I’ll take Watson and Golden vs. Gonzalez and Davis over Hollins and Douglas vs. Keisean Nixon and Brandon Cisse. In a close game, the Packers will fail to run out the clock but the defense will save the day. And they’ll need it, with the Bears and Lions favored to win their games against the Buccaneers and Dolphins, respectively, while the first-place Vikings are underdogs against Buffalo. Bill’s Prediction: Packers 24, Patriots 20. Bill’s Record: 6-2. Jacob Westendorf’s Packers-Patriots Prediction Everything outside of the field favors New England in this game with the return of Rob Gronkowski and Tom Brady, which has been discussed all week. The reality on the field, however, is that the Packers have more healthy players than the Patriots do. The Patriots are missing their top two receivers and their starting tight end is going to be hobbled, at minimum, if he can play. Drake Maye and Jordon Love are both being asked to carry a heavy load, but Love has a better supporting cast around him. In addition, Jonathan Gannon should be able to create enough confusion for Maye to make a couple of mistakes that swing the game in the Packers’ favor. Jacob’s Prediction: Packers 24, Patriots 17. Jacob’s Record: 5-3. picks.blurb: These Are the Three Factors Packers Must Take Advantage of to Beat Patriots Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers have their eyes on the Super Bowl. So do the New England Patriots, who lost in last year’s Super Bowl. On Sunday, these storied teams will collide in Foxborough in what is truly a measuring-stick game for the Packers. The Patriots are three-point favorites. With Tom Brady on the call and Rob Gronkowski being inducted into the team’s Hall of Fame, here are three reasons why the Packers will spoil the party and earn a statement win. 1. Depleted Patriots Offense The Patriots reached the Super Bowl last year despite the lack of a legit threat at receiver. So, they attempted to rectify that problem by signing Romeo Doubs, who had a solid four seasons with the Packers, and trading for A.J. Brown, a three-time Pro Bowler who had surpassed 1,000 yards in six of his first seven seasons. Neither player will be on the field for this game, though. Doubs is on injured reserve with a shoulder injury and Brown is out again with a knee injury. Combined with the questionable status of top tight end Hunter Henry, who leads the team in receptions, the Packers’ strong defense will face a diluted New England attack. Without Brown and Doubs and with Henry limited to eight snaps with an injured foot, the Patriots needed to rally past the lowly Dolphins last week. The Patriots were held to merely 313 yards. The key for the Packers will be limiting the Rhamondre Stevenson-led running game and putting the pressure on New England’s passing game to make plays against a Packers defense that ranks fourth in opponent passer rating. “I think first of all, he’s an elite quarterback in the pocket, out of the pocket,” cornerback Brandon Cisse said of Drake Maye. “He’s extremely dangerous. He can make any throw. Obviously, he’s super-smart. “They got a great offensive coordinator, great receivers, great playmakers around him and, obviously, when the run game’s going they can do everything and they can throw it just as good as they can run it. So, we’re going to have our hands full for sure and got to make sure that we’re ready to play.” Prediction: The Patriots are going to have a hard time stringing together sustained success on offense. 2. Drake Maye May Screw Up Patriots quarterback Drake Maye is one of the best in the business. He was one vote away from winning NFL MVP last year. However, unless you’re one of the undisputed elite quarterbacks, a quarterback oftentimes is only as good as his supporting cast. So, while Maye is seventh in completion percentage, third in yards per attempt and fifth in touchdowns, only three quarterbacks have thrown more than Maye’s eight interceptions and his six fumbles are one off the unwelcome NFL lead. “I think speaking from playing zone coverage, they’ve got great eyes,” Maye told reporters this week. “They got eyes on the quarterback, they make plays on the football. They can, obviously, catch well. The safeties are great players. They do a lot of things well and they read the quarterback very well, mix up in zone looks. Tip balls have turned into picks that they’ve shown. “So, they’ve just had a habit of creating turnovers in the pocket with the quarterback. They have got some free rushers’ help, too, of the quarterback panicking and trying to fit some stuff to tight windows. They’re good at keeping you in some negative plays. They make you go longer distances. It’s hard.” In the Patriots’ three losses, Maye has thrown three touchdowns vs. six interceptions. In the five wins, it’s 12 touchdowns and two interceptions. His eight interceptions equal last year’s total (in less than half the attempts) are only two off his total from his rookie season in 2024. Prediction: It only takes one big mistake to swing a game between equal teams. Based on this season, Maye is more apt to make that mistake. 3. Turnovers (And Taking Advantage of Them) “The ball” is the most important thing in the sport, coach Matt LaFleur likes to say. Teams that take away and protect the ball tend to win; teams that don’t tend to lose. The Packers are tied for fourth in the league at plus-4 in turnovers. After creating only 14 takeaways last season – when Micah Parsons was on the field for 14 games – they rank second in the league with 15 takeaways this season. The Patriots this year are minus-7 overall; only the white-flag-of-surrender-waving Colts are worse at minus-11. Their 15 giveaways are the third-most in the league. Added together, you get this chart. Points Off Turnovers through Week 8 pic.twitter.com/UmVq9xw7uU The Packers are third in the league by scoring 52 points off takeaways; the Patriots are tied for 23rd with 20 points off takeaways. Green Bay’s aggressive, playmaking defense works hand-in-hand with quarterback Jordan Love’s aggressive, playmaking approach to the position. “Nobody’s had more 20-yard pass plays,” Patriots coach Mike Vrabel told reporters on Wednesday. “(Love is) a quarterback that’s wildly efficient. He has a few off-days, but they’re few and far between. They throw shots. They’ve, obviously, great speed on the edges. They have an excellent tight end, Tucker Kraft, and now getting [Josh] Jacobs back, it seems like they’re trying to work him back in there a little bit more and see what he can do for them in the red zone and things like that. I think they’ve protected better the last few games. “I think that when one of your best players for them is their quarterback, or their best player, that’s an emphasis that they try to make because when you give him time, he’s able to find [Matthew] Golden, [Christian] Watson or Tucker Kraft. Defensively, very physical. They have the second-most negative plays and created the second-most negative plays in the league. Seventeen percent of their drives end in a turnover, so that leads the league, as well.” Love is cooking. He and Kirk Cousins are the only quarterbacks with at least two touchdown passes in seven games this season. “Our goal every week is to go 1-0, and this is a very good team,” Love said. “Like you mentioned, they were in the Super Bowl last year for a reason. They’re very good in, really, all three phases. They got an elite defense. I think they do a lot of things really well. They got two really good corners on the outside. “Yeah, I got a lot of respect for them. It’s always a good test, but I think the goal for us to see how we can go out there and execute the plan, and the goal is to come away victorious. We know to put ourselves in the best position late in the season. We got to really just win every game, and that’s the mindset of going 1-0 every week. It’ll be a good test for us.” Prediction: The Packers have at least two takeaways in five consecutive games. If they can do it again, they’ll win. Drake Maye struggled against the Seahawks (fifth), Steelers (sixth), and Jaguars (fourth), completing just 63.8% of his passes with one touchdown and six interceptions. Packers defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon also gets extra prep time for a New England offense without wide receiver A.J. Brown and possibly without Mack Hollins and tight end Hunter Henry . The Patriots are 3-point favorites on the spread (Patriots -3), with the over/under set at 44.5 (-112o / -108u). The Patriots are -170 favorites on the moneyline and the Packers are +142 underdogs. Let's get into my Packers vs Patriots Week 9 prediction . Packers vs Patriots pick: Packers +3 (-110) My Packers vs Patriots best bet is on Green Bay to cover the spread. Packers vs Patriots Odds Packers vs Patriots Spread : Packers +3 (-105), Patriots -3 (-115) Packers vs Patriots Over/Under : 44.5 (-112o / -108u) Packers vs Patriots Moneyline : Packers +142, Patriots -170 Packers vs Patriots Week 9 Preview The Packers under head coach Matt LaFleur have been an excellent team to back when they are priced as underdogs. LaFleur has covered 65.1% of all games when his team is catching points, and I believe this is another very good spot for Green Bay to potentially steal a victory. The narrative surrounding the Packers offense has to do with their lack of pass protection, as every mention of their future outlook as a Super Bowl contender is usually followed by a comment regarding their offensive line issues. Jordan Love is navigating those issues quite well, as it may be surprising to some that he has just a 32% pressure rate on all of his dropbacks. Only seven quarterbacks with 200 or more dropbacks have faced pressure less often than Love this season. We already know Green Bay struggles to run the football effectively, and that data point is completely baked into the line here. Sure, most of the offensive success for this team is squarely on the shoulders of Love, but that is something I am completely comfortable with against a Patriots team that ranks 26th in quick pressure percentage. Quick pressures occur within 2.5 seconds of the snap, and it is not something I am concerned about happening regularly in this matchup. If there is a signal caller who will be under constant duress in this game, it is likely to be Drake Maye . Maye has regained his MVP-level play from a season ago, but protection issues that plagued this team in the playoffs remain. The 44% pressure rate allowed by the New England offensive line is the highest rate league-wide. The Packers are generating pressure at the 12th-highest rate, but more importantly, they are converting those pressures into sacks. Green Bay has 22 sacks on the season, the sixth-most in the NFL. While the Packers' pass rush is undoubtedly above average, it has been the coverage in the secondary that has been this defense's biggest strength. Green Bay allows just 6.2 yards per pass attempt (fifth-best) while also ranking among the top five pass defenses in expected points added (EPA) per pass against. During Maye's hot streak, he has been doing his best work when throwing down the field. Maye leads the league in touchdown passes of 20 or more yards downfield this season, in addition to being efficient in the intermediate areas of the field. Over the past five weeks, Maye has completed 67% of his throws that have traveled more than 10 yards past the line of scrimmage. However, it is worth noting he has not played the most difficult slate of defenses during that stretch. The Packers are a completely different animal defensively than the teams Maye has shredded in recent weeks. During that same span of five games, Green Bay is second in the league in defensive EPA. The Packers specialize in limiting explosive plays — allowing the third-fewest of any defense in football. On throws 10 or more yards downfield, the Packers have allowed opposing quarterbacks to complete just 44% of their passes, generating seven interceptions while allowing just two touchdowns. The Patriots are not equipped to pressure Love as often as they need to, but the Packers do possess the tools to halt numerous New England possessions with their sticky coverage and timely pass rush led by Devonte Wyatt and Lukas Van Ness . Packers vs Patriots Spread Prediction, Betting Analysis Jordan Love and Drake Maye are in good form — both rank inside the top 12 of qualifying quarterbacks in adjusted net yards per attempt, have passer ratings that exceed 105.0 when kept clean and boast identical big-time throw rates. Let's call it a wash at quarterback. The team protecting their passer more cleanly also happens to be the team with the decided advantage defensively. Getting three points with the Packers in this spot is a tremendous value. Add in Matt LaFleur's success rate at covering the number as an underdog during his tenure as Packers head coach, and this may be one of my strongest positions of the NFL season thus far. The Jets are not known for being a stout defense, but they are serviceable and gave Las Vegas fits for the entire first half, holding the Raiders to 97 total yards. Still, Zuhn looked like he may be the Raiders' best option at right guard for the rest of the season. Sunday's matchup against the 49ers will be much more telling, as San Francisco's defense is much more of a challenge than New York's. It will be interesting to see how Zuhn does at guard against one of the toughest teams the Raiders will face this season. Sep 13, 2026; Paradise, Nevada, USA; Las Vegas Raiders guard Trey Zuhn III (66) runs onto the field during the game against the Miami Dolphins at Allegiant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: David Brytus-Imagn Images. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Recent Shakeups May Last Another Week, or More Recent Shakeups May Last Another Week, or More Given their success last week, even against the Jets, Las Vegas would be wise to stick with those changes for an additional week to get another look at how well they work. If Zuhn plays well against the 49ers, the starting right guard position is his to lose. Starting Zuhn at right guard wasn't the only change Las Vegas made against the Jets. They also started rookie running back Mike Washington over Ashton Jeanty. The Raiders cannot afford to sit Jeanty for an entire game, as he is far too valuable catching the ball out of the backfield. Still, the way they successfully used Washington on the ground and Jeanty through the air against the Jets is worth building upon in Week 9 against the 49ers. Oct 25, 2026; Paradise, Nevada, USA; Las Vegas Raiders running back Mike Washington Jr. (4) rushes the ball against the Los Angeles Rams sin the first half at Allegiant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Ahead of the team's road matchup against the 49ers, offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko praised Washington's Week 8 outing. Ahead of the team's road matchup against the 49ers, offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko praised Washington's Week 8 outing. “He’s somebody that continues to improve, really works his craft. He wants to get better at each and every single thing he does, whether it’s fitting his hands up, his eyes, everything coming out. It’s all the little fundamental things that we talk about. It’s stuff that he wants to get better at, improve on, and that’ll allow him to become a more successful player,” Janocko said earlier this week. “Running the ball is a full team thing. The greatest thing about football in general is that it’s 11 as one on every single play. So, it takes all 11 for everybody to be successful." Cornerback Darien Porter returned to practice this week after playing only one play against the New York Jets last Sunday. He is officially listed as questionable heading into Week 9. However, speed is arguably Porter's greatest asset on the field, and he is dealing with a groin injury. A groin injury can linger. Despite being listed as questionable, Kubiak and defensive coordinator Rob Leonard may decide not to risk damage to Porter's long-term health in a game where they already face an uphill battle. Las Vegas faced a similar decision earlier this season, when they could have rested running back Ashton Jeanty against a New England Patriots team that was missing more than five players before their matchup ended. The Raiders need Porter beyond just this week. Resting Porter on Sunday is far from ideal for Sunday's game, but may be best for his career, depending on the severity of his injury and how much progress he made on it during the week. Porter sitting out would offer a valuable opportunity to other corners on the roster. Porter may very well start against the 49ers. Regardless, rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses is sure to see significant playing time. Heading into Sunday, Masses could be in for another action-packed day, who has had extreme highs and lows during this season. “I think it’s always a moving target. See where your team’s at, and who’s playing the best ball at the time. And it’s a 17-game regular season where things change every week. And [there have] been changes at guard," Kubiak said earlier this week. "[We have] changed up front defensively. Changed at corner, and that’s the NFL. We have a young roster, and we’re going to give guys opportunities and see what fits us best." The 49ers are 8.5-point favorites on the spread, with the over/under set at 51.5 total points. San Francisco is a -440 moneyline favorite to win outright, while Las Vegas is a +340 underdog. Let's get into my Raiders vs 49ers predictions and player props . Raiders vs. 49ers Picks: Ashton Jeanty Over 27.5 Rushing Yards | Christian McCaffrey Over 60.5 Rushing Yards My Raiders vs. 49ers best bets are two props for Ashton Jeanty and Christian McCaffrey — both overs on their rushing yards. But a collapse by the Jets kept Kirk Cousins in the driver's seat, and the veteran is expected to start again on Sunday. Despite the Raiders putting up 38 points, one storyline stole the headlines: Mike Washington Jr. handled 25 carries. Ashton Jeanty? Just two. Could that be tied to Jeanty's comments about the Jets' lack of interest in tackling in the week leading up to the game? Possibly. But Jeanty has also been largely inefficient, averaging just 2.2 yards per carry over the previous three weeks. The soft benching could serve as a wake-up call for Jeanty, although Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak still expects the workload split between Jeanty and Washington to vary week to week. I expect Jeanty to get a much larger share of the carries today. Washington didn't exactly make the most of his opportunity, averaging just 3.3 yards per carry on 25 attempts against New York. Despite a struggling run game, Cousins has kept the offense competitive. The Raiders rank sixth in the NFL in scoring at 27.6 points per game, with much of that production going through tight end Brock Bowers , who is averaging 91.2 receiving yards per game. Tre Tucker has emerged as a reliable receiving option thanks to his speed, but the rest of the wide receiver room remains thin. Jalen Nailor has gradually settled into the WR2 role, while Jack Bech continues to work his way back from injury. Defensively, the Raiders can't stop a nosebleed. Opponents have scored at least 30 points against Las Vegas in each of the last five weeks. The Raiders rank in the bottom three in both yards allowed per game (381.9) and points allowed per game (28.8). The 49ers' Week 8 bye came at the perfect time as they continue to deal with one of the most injury-riddled offenses in football. After opening the season with six straight wins, San Francisco fell to Atlanta. Christian McCaffrey battled through an injury and missed a large portion of the game, while the 49ers were also without Deebo Samuel and Mike Evans . Samuel and Evans are not expected to return Sunday, but the 49ers should get Demarcus Robinson back. McCaffrey also benefits from the extra rest and is good to go — a massive boost for an offense that runs through him. Despite all the injuries, the 49ers' offense continues to hum. Brock Purdy is playing like an MVP candidate, and San Francisco ranks among the league's top five in scoring at 28.1 points per game. However, it's the defense that has taken the biggest step forward this season. Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw have elevated the linebacker group, while the midseason acquisition of DeForest Buckner gives the defensive line another dimension. Nick Bosa , who hasn't played since Week 2, also returns from injury today. Allowing fewer than 20 points per game, San Francisco may finally have the pieces to chase that elusive Super Bowl trophy. When healthy, this team can be a force to be reckoned with. Raiders vs 49ers Player Props, Picks There are two props I like in this one. The first is ugly and comes with plenty of uncertainty, but I'm willing to take the risk. I refuse to believe Klint Kubiak is going to make the same mistake twice and leave Ashton Jeanty behind Mike Washington Jr. on the depth chart. There's plenty of speculation surrounding this team, but Washington is not the answer. In fact, he's tied with Jacoby Brissett in broken tackles this season (one). Jeanty is far more explosive than Washington, particularly as a pass catcher. Has the Raiders' run game been a problem all season? Absolutely. But Jeanty's rushing yards prop set at 27.5 is simply too low for me to pass up. I'll hold my nose and back Jeanty, even with the Raiders entering as double-digit underdogs. The second prop centers around Christian McCaffrey. As always, the biggest concern with the superstar is injury risk. However, McCaffrey is coming off a bye week and got Wednesday off, which is standard treatment for many veteran players. He returned to practice Thursday and practiced in full on Friday. The Raiders' run defense has been putrid. We just saw Braelon Allen average 7.0 yards per carry against them last week, marking the seventh consecutive week an opponent has rushed for at least 100 yards. Las Vegas is currently allowing 5.31 yards per carry. Not only should the 49ers have plenty of success against this defense, but the game script could also lead to a more run-heavy approach. McCaffrey is averaging 4.6 yards per carry and has cleared this rushing yards line (60.5) in all five games in which he's played at least 55% of the snaps. Expect a fresher McCaffrey and plenty of success on the ground. away.headline: Raiders' Thursday Injury Report Gives Reason for Cautious Optimism
away.blurb: On Wednesday, the official injury report listed defensive tackles Thomas Booker and Folorunso Fatukasi and tight end Ian Thomas as limited participants. Cornerback Darien Porter missed Wednesday's practice with a groin injury he suffered against the Jets. On Thursday, Las Vegas' injury report remained minimal. Porter returned to practice on Thursday, which is good news for the Raiders' young defensive backfield. He was a limited participant, and Thomas was a full participant. Booker did not practice on Thursday. Dont'e Thornton was limited as well. Raiders' Thursday Injury Report Gives Reason for Cautious Optimism Skip to main content SI.COM The Las Vegas Raiders are just a few days away from facing the San Francisco 49ers on the road. Las Vegas went back to work on Thursday, looking to build upon their Week 9 win over the New York Jets. Las Vegas' success this season has largely depended on the quality of the opponent they face. The Raiders have played well enough to beat four of the league's worst teams, but have struggled against the league's elite, which the 49ers are. Still, those four wins are more than the Raiders had all last season, and they are unquestionably better than last season. It may have been against the Jets, but Las Vegas aims to translate its second-half success against New York to this Sunday against the 49ers. After struggling in the third quarter all season, the Raiders' offense exploded against the Jets. In Week 8, Kirk Cousins led the Raiders downfield to score on their first offensive drive after halftime for the first time all season. It was more than impactful, as it led to Las Vegas producing their best third quarter of the season. The Raiders must continue to play well on offense to help their defense. “I think the first play of the second half might have been the throw to Brock [Bowers], and I thought that was a key play in the game and a great call by our coaches, and that whole drive, to finish that drive, it got us right back in the game, which we needed, very important," Cousins said earlier this week. “If you punt and they go down and score, it could be a whole different story. So, it’s very important, and we’ve got to be really strong in the third quarter the rest of the way. And I felt we have continued, last week in the fourth quarter, continuing to play well in the fourth quarter. But it’s a four-quarter game. You’ve got to do it, all four of them.” Throughout the rest of the season, Las Vegas needs the Cousins who showed up in the third and fourth quarters against the Jets to show up in each of their next three games. Moving forward, they will need that version of Cousins and their offense even before the third quarter. Fatukasi was a full participant as well. Based on their injury report, Las Vegas appears to be the healthiest it has been this season, as their Week 1 injury report listed stars Ashton Jeanty and Brock Bowers. That, in theory, would lead to even more potential success for Arizona. However, there's two issues. The Cardinals are running into a Seahawks defense very much looking to send a message after falling to the Chicago Bears on Monday Night Football last week. A Seattle defense, one that's had Arizona's number in recent years, is down some notable names — but play-caller Mike Macdonald still deserves the nod here until he doesn't in this matchup. Chicago is on a three-game win streak since Williams returned from a hamstring injury, and the Bears are in position to contend for a second consecutive NFC North title. They now enter this week ranked inside the top seven in every rushing metric, second in opponent EPA per play, and third in opponent success rate. We don't currently know what sort of form Baker Mayfield is in, but if he's in peak form when the Bucs need him to take to the air, Tampa Bay is going to be an extremely dangerous team. I have little bad to say about the Bears, who have proven me wrong about my preseason evaluation of them. What I do think is that this is a sell-high spot on a short week after an emotional win on Monday Night Football. MacMillan may think this is an upset spot for the Bucs, but the Bears have been one of the best offenses in the league when Williams is healthy and are 4-0 straight up when he starts and finishes a game this season. I think there’s a path for Tampa Bay to cover – it does have the No. 1 defense in the league in EPA/Play – but I’m taking the Bears to win this game at home. Mayfield’s lack of passing the last two weeks is certainly a concern when assessing how well he’s recovered from a thumb injury that cost him multiple games. As dominant as the Vikings defense has been, Bills quarterback Josh Allen presents a unique challenge for Brian Flores' blitz-focused stop unit. Minnesota has yet to face a QB who can move away from pressure, extend plays, and scramble like Allen. The Vikings' QB competition so far has been primarily pocket passers. Based on records, at least, it is a potential Super Bowl preview. Both teams are 6-1, Buffalo despite a porous defense and Minnesota despite an inept offense. Here is my SGP for Monday's primetime festivities, which get underway at 8:15 pm ET on ESPN. Also be sure to check out our full Bills vs Vikings predictions . Bills -3 (-118) James Cook III Over 83.5 rushing yards (-114) James Cook III to score a touchdown (-105) Carson Wentz Over 209.5 passing yards (-113) Parlay odds: +650 Part of the value in a Same Game Parlay, of course, is that all of its components can be correlated if you so choose. That is some of the plan here, as Buffalo running back James Cook having a big night would obviously work well with a Bills win and cover. At the same time, plays that aren’t correlated drive up the overall payout of the parlay. That is the case with backing Minnesota quarterback Carson Wentz to throw for his fair share of yards. But even if he does, there is no reason why the visitors can’t take care of business. Let’s break down each of the three legs. NFL SGP Pick: Bills -3 (-105) This should be a fascinating matchup of strength vs. strength and weakness vs. weakness. The Bills’ offense is amazing, but the Vikings bring one of the best defenses to the table; the Vikings’ offense stinks, but the Bills have a defense that can give up points to anyone. In this case, I’m rolling with offense. Buffalo is #1 in the entire NFL in scoring (33.3 points per game) and #2 in yards (393.1 per game). Former offensive coordinator Joe Brady is now the head coach, and if anything Josh Allen has gotten even better. Allen, who has accounted for 20 total touchdowns (11 passing, nine rushing) is currently the first or second favorite to earn NFL MVP honors depending on the sportsbook. Minnesota is coming off a tough, physical matchup against NFC North rival Detroit and it resulted in the Vikings’ first loss of the season – an ugly 19-15 decision. Yes, their 6-1 record is still impressive, but they have not defeated anyone good since Week 2. Kyler Murray is out with a hamstring injury, so Carson Wentz will be under center for the home side. Wentz may not be the worst backup in the world, but 2017 ain’t walkin’ through that door. To say that this isn’t the MVP contender version of Wentz would be a gross understatement. picks.blurb: Bills vs. Vikings bold predictions for Week 9 Monday Night Football - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football NFL Week 9 updates Luka has tight back Rivers to coach NC State CFB winners and losers Bills vs. Vikings bold predictions for Week 9 Monday Night Football Garrett Kerman, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 3, 2026 at 5:57 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Two 6-1 teams enter Monday Night Football with very different questions. Can the Buffalo Bills keep rolling against the NFL's stingiest defense? Can the Minnesota Vikings generate enough offense to avoid wasting another strong defensive performance? Buffalo visits U.S. Bank Stadium on November 9 following a 36–10 victory over Baltimore. Minnesota returns home after Detroit ended its unbeaten start with a 19–15 win. The Bills opened as three-point favorites, setting up a compelling clash between offensive firepower and defensive disruption. These three predictions anticipate a departure from Minnesota's usual defensive script, explosive passing, costly mistakes and a dramatic finish that hands Buffalo its second defeat. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Justin Jefferson explodes for 175 yards and two touchdowns Matt Krohn-Imagn Images Jefferson will deliver the performance Minnesota has been waiting for, finishing with at least 175 receiving yards and two touchdowns. Jefferson caught five passes for 33 yards and a touchdown against Detroit and enters Week 9 without a 100-yard receiving game. Buffalo presents an opportunity to change that. Its defense ranks 30th against the pass, making this a matchup Minnesota should attack rather than approach conservatively. The Vikings need to manufacture touches before asking Jefferson to win difficult downfield assignments. Motion, condensed formations and crossing routes would help create cleaner releases and give the quarterback defined throwing windows. The bigger gains should follow when Buffalo adjusts to those shorter completions. One double move or broken coverage could turn a productive evening into a spectacular one. Quarterback availability remains important. Kyler Murray is managing hamstring tightness , with Carson Wentz the likely alternative if Murray cannot play. Expect Minnesota to make its best receiver the centerpiece, not merely a name opponents must account for. Josh Allen accounts for four touchdowns but commits three turnovers Allen will produce enough spectacular plays to keep Buffalo dangerous and enough mistakes to give Minnesota control of the outcome. The bold prediction is four total touchdowns alongside three turnovers, including at least two interceptions. https://twitter.com/search?q=josh%20allen&src=typed_query&f=top Minnesota's defense provides the foundation for that aggressive forecast. Entering Week 9, the Vikings lead the league in points allowed per game at 13.3, quarterback pressure rate at 45.8 percent and sack percentage at 10.96 percent. Pressure alone will not neutralize Allen. His ability to escape the pocket can turn a successful blitz into a defensive emergency, particularly when coverage players must chase receivers across the field. That creates the central tension. Minnesota will win several snaps decisively, but Allen will punish a few failed pressure attempts with explosive completions or scrambling opportunities. The turnovers will come when he tries to rescue plays that should end with a throwaway. Disguised coverage behind an apparent blitz can invite exactly that kind of aggressive decision. Buffalo's offensive line also bears watching. Right tackle Spencer Brown's availability is a concern entering the matchup, potentially complicating protection against Minnesota's pressure packages. Allen will remain the game's most dangerous improviser. On this night, improvisation will carry a substantial price. Minnesota wins 38–35 on a last-second field goal The final bold prediction ties those individual performances together: Minnesota wins a shootout with a field goal as time expires. A 38–35 result would produce 73 points, comfortably exceeding the opening total of 46.5. It would also represent a dramatic departure from the Vikings' defensive scoring average. The logic is not that Minnesota suddenly becomes a bad defense. Turnovers and explosive plays can produce points without requiring long, methodical drives. Jefferson's breakout keeps the Vikings moving, while Allen repeatedly answers before one late mistake gives Minnesota the deciding possession. After losing its unbeaten record, Minnesota will respond with its most convincing offensive statement and a victory that reinforces its place among the league's contenders. picks.headline: Minnesota Vikings Receive Bold Prediction for Game Against Buffalo Bills
picks.blurb: Minnesota Vikings Receive Bold Prediction for Game Against Buffalo Bills - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football NFL Week 9 updates Luka has tight back Rivers to coach NC State CFB winners and losers Minnesota Vikings Receive Bold Prediction for Game Against Buffalo Bills (Gregory Fisher-USA TODAY Sports) Joey Hickey · Roundtable Sports Thu, November 5, 2026 at 6:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Minnesota Vikings (6-1) have a pivotal matchup on Monday Night Football against the Buffalo Bills. And while losing the game wouldn't make them a pretender, winning the game could solidify the Vikings as contenders. Minnesota has played great defense through seven games, but the offense has been lacking. Now, fans are looking for the team to show improvement on offense. If it doesn't happen, we could see the team explore changes on offense. Vikings Wire's Andrew Harbaugh predicts that Vikings backup quarterback Carson Wentz will see playing time in Monday night's game against the Buffalo Bills. Here's some of what Harbaugh had to say about his chances to take the field for Minnesota in the game. "Kyler Murray has played poorly enough this season and has not shown a real grasp of the offense or the players' tendencies within it. Carson Wentz has not been a rockstar, but he has been more than serviceable for the Vikings when he has played. I predict that the first half could be rough for the Vikings' offense, and at halftime Kevin O'Connell tries to give the offense a spark with a quarterback change." Harbaugh adds that it could be a breakout day for another Vikings player. He has star Vikings wideout Justin Jefferson catching two touchdown passes in the matchup. Here's what he had to say on the breakout. "Justin Jefferson has started to be a bit more vocal about how he feels about the offense being so quiet. I think they make it a point to get him going early in the game, and then by the end of the night he has two touchdowns. They have to get him involved more; the offense goes as Justin Jefferson goes, after all. If they do not use him more soon, then ideas and outside voices are going to start getting louder." Jefferson's frustrations have drawn questions about the player throwing him the football. It's not surprising that there have been questions given all the pieces that the Vikings have on offense. It's not that starting quarterback Kyler Murray has been awful. The offense has been awful, though. Some believe a change at quarterback is necessary to bring a spark. Maybe a change at quarterback isn't the fix, but something will need to change for the offense to start moving the football. If it doesn't the Vikings will have squandered what could be one of the NFL's best defenses of the last decade. We'll keep a close eye on what moves head coach Kevin O'Connell makes when the matchup gets underway with Buffalo.
