picks.blurb: NFL Insider Makes Bold Prediction About Vikings Offensive Direction in Week 9 vs. Bills - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football NFL Week 9 updates Luka has tight back Rivers to coach NC State CFB winners and losers Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kevin O'Connell has spent the week calling Kyler Murray his starter, but a hamstring may make that call for him. NFL Network insider Tom Pelissero said Thursday on KFAN's Power Trip Morning Show that he expects Carson Wentz to start for the 6-1 Minnesota Vikings against the Buffalo Bills on Monday night, days after Murray struggled through the loss in Detroit . "I would lean toward it being Carson Wentz," Pelissero said on KFAN . He described the hamstring as legitimate but not major, and said Minnesota may not want to risk a quarterback who relies on his legs at less than full speed. Carson Wentz has already won two games Nov 1, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Minnesota Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell talks to quarterback Kyler Murray (1) during the third quarter against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field.Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Wentz isn't a stranger to this offense. He played most of the 39-22 opener against Green Bay after replacing Murray early and threw three touchdown passes, then started the 9-3 win in Chicago. He has 276 passing yards and no interceptions this season, and Minnesota won both games. Those wins weren't pretty, though. The offense scored nine points at Soldier Field, and Wentz was sacked six times across the two games. Behind a line that has allowed 21 sacks, the Vikings would be trading mobility for a quarterback who has to get the ball out on time. Murray has 1,022 passing yards, five touchdown passes and three interceptions, and he's been sacked 15 times. He has also run for 167 yards on 29 carries, which is why a sore hamstring matters more for him than it would for most quarterbacks. O'Connell said Monday he isn't considering a performance benching and Murray is still the starter when healthy, per ESPN. "I don't think we're there yet," he said of a possible absence , adding that he would keep getting updates from the medical staff. Pelissero's take lands after Nick Kostos argued the Vikings can't keep waiting on Murray . Pelissero also said he sees a low chance of a major trade before the Nov. 10 deadline, which leaves the job between the two quarterbacks already in the building. Either one draws a tough assignment. Buffalo's Greg Rousseau has seven sacks, and Josh Allen brings the NFL's most efficient offense to U.S. Bank Stadium, so Brian Flores' defense may need to carry the night again. O'Connell's Thursday press availability should offer the next clue. The receiver pulled up while running a deep route late in the first quarter. He went to the ground and was ruled out for the remainder of the game. Palmer has already missed time this season because of a shoulder injury that kept him out of Buffalo's Week 5 victory over the Rams. The Bills also listed Keon Coleman as limited for the second consecutive day because of a shoulder injury. D.J. Moore remained limited with the shoulder injury that previously cost him two games. Moore returned against Baltimore but also hyperextended his knee during the fourth quarter. Kincaid was a full participant Friday after being limited Thursday because of a chest injury. The Bills also opened the 21-day practice window for defensive back Jordan Hancock on Thursday. Hancock, who has been on injured reserve since September because of a hamstring injury, remained limited Friday. The Vikings also practiced without wide receiver Jauan Jennings on Friday after he was limited Thursday because of a calf injury. Darrisaw was limited Thursday but returned to full practice Friday. Van Ginkel, who is tied for fifth in the NFL with 6.5 sacks, remained limited with a chest injury. He recorded 2.5 sacks against Detroit on Sunday. Claiborne is currently in his 21-day return-to-practice window. home.headline: Bills’ Week 9 injury report vs. Vikings: Can Buffalo survive O-line injuries vs. Brian Flores?
home.blurb: Dawkins missed practice throughout the week, and sat out the last three days, including Saturday with a rib injury. He is listed as doubtful on the injury report. Anderson has an ankle issue. While he did not practice Thursday or Friday, he was on the field in a limited fashion Saturday with his teammates. The Bills also list him as questionable. Brown seems to be in a much better position than either of the other two offensive linemen. He has a back injury, but he was a limited participant on Thursday and Friday. He jumped up to a full participant Saturday. In addition to the offensive line issues that the Bills are going to try to overcome, nose tackle Greg Gaines is questionable with a calf injury and wide receiver Josh Palmer is out with a hamstring issue. The Buffalo Bills (6-1) are on a mission this year to get the job done in the regular season and regain the AFC East title after losing it last year to the New England Patriots. That’s just the regular-season goal. The full-year goal is to represent the AFC in the Super Bowl and win it for the first time in team history. This week’s game against the Minnesota Vikings (6-1) represents the dramatic positioning of the Bills as the best offensive team in the NFL meeting the best defense in the league. The Monday night setting at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis means the whole world — at least from the NFL’s perspective — will be watching. In addition to the best vs. best aspect, the game also features the Bills’ struggling defense against the Vikings moribund offense. If either one of those units can step up in this game, it could go a long way towards determining the winner of this matchup. Both sides have significant injuries. The homestanding Vikings have benched starting QB Kyler Murray because he has a hamstring injury and backup Carson Wentz has been tapped on the shoulder by head coach Kevin O’Connell to start the game. Offensive line issues have hit the Bills The Bills have a slew of injuries , primarily on the offensive line. Three of the Bills starters on the offensive line are listed on the team’s substantial injury report. They include left tackle Dion Dawkins , left guard Alec Anderson and right tackle Spencer Brown. Josh Allen needs solid OL performance against Vikings’ relentless D The Bills have not seen a defense like the one the Vikings present on an every-game basis. Their blitzing ways is a challenge for every opposing quarterback and offensive coordinator, and that means it should be somewhat difficult for Allen and Pete Carmichael Jr. However, Allen is capable of delivering big plays even when he is under pressure. If the Vikings pass rush that consists of key sackers Dallas Turner and Andrew Van Ginkel get their hands on Allen, they must put him on the ground. It is much tougher to finish a sack on Allen than nearly any quarterback in the league because of his size and strength. home.blurb: Buffalo Bills head coach Joe Brady ruled out one player and listed five others as questionable for Monday night's game at the Vikings. WR Joshua Palmer (hamstring) will be out, while LT Dion Dawkins (ribs), LG Alec Anderson (ankle), DB Jordan Hancock (hamstring), DL Greg Gaines (calf) and WR Tyrell Shavers (knee) will all be questionable. Palmer did not practice all week after leaving last week's game due to injury, though Brady said the receiver is not a candidate for injured reserve at this point. If Shavers or Hancock were to play, the team would have to activate them from IR by Monday afternoon. Hancock had his 21-day practice window opened this week has been a limited participant; Shavers has been a full participant. "There's certain positions that have played enough football that I believe they can go out there and do their job, certain people that can do their job without the practice," Brady said. Five players will be questionable for Sunday's matchup against the Raiders. home.blurb: In a positive development, Brown began the practice week by participating in a limited capacity, but back injuries can be fickle to say the least. Offensive starters DJ Moore, Keon Coleman and Dalton Kincaid were all limited participants on Thursday. All three skill players were seen wearing red non-contact jerseys during the media-viewing portion of practice ( h/t WGR's Sal Capaccio ). Along with Dawkins and Anderson, there were three more non-participants. Wide receiver Josh Palmer is seemingly looking at a multi-week absence after pulling his hamstring in Week 8 . Defensive tackle Greg Gaines, who was banged up in practice last week, remains out. Third-down running back Ty Johnson missed Thursday's practice due to illness. Despite being limited, and wearing a red jersey as a precaution, the outlook is nothing but positive for Moore. Dawkins was a surprise addition to the injury report as he appeared to come out of Sunday's game intact. He sat out the last possession, missing four snaps, but so did Allen and starting center Connor McGovern. Veteran guard Austin Corbett, who subbed in for the Allen touchdown rush, would start on Monday if Anderson is unavailable. Coleman is limited by a shoulder, which explains the red non-contact jersey he dawned on Thursday. It's unknown at which point in the game the injury occurred. He led all Bills' wide receivers with 63 snaps.
